In the Elder Days, when the Two Trees of Valinor were slain and their light failed, Morgoth the great Enemy stole the Silmarils — the three holy jewels wrought by Fëanor, in which that light yet lived — and fled north to Angband, his fortress of iron beneath the triple peaks of Thangorodrim. There he set the Jewels in an iron crown and sat enthroned in darkness, walled about by orcs, balrogs, and dragons.

For the Silmarils Fëanor swore his terrible Oath, and the Noldor forsook the Blessed Realm and came in exile to Beleriand to make war upon the Enemy. They raised proud kingdoms and held Angband under siege through long years — yet their valour was ever shadowed by the Kinslaying at Alqualondë and the Doom of Mandos that followed them.

They did not fight alone. The Sindar, Grey-elves who dwelt beneath the stars of Beleriand long before the Noldor came, took up arms in the Elven realms and at the Havens of the Falas — though hidden Doriath, girdled by the power of Melian, held apart behind its enchanted bounds. The Naugrim, Dwarves of the Blue Mountains, forged matchless mail and axes and marched to the great battles. And the Edain, the first Men over the mountains, swore friendship to the Eldar and spent their brief, valiant lives in the war, winning undying renown.

The tide cities were built around a weather engine maintained by nine custodians. It measured pressure, moved water, and gave the settlements time to prepare for storms. Varkesh took control of the lower works and locked three dawnseeds into his crown assembly. The engine failed aboveground while its power served him below. You are Eralen, a former flood marshal recovered by the recall loom after the evacuation of Aster Quay. Your memories are incomplete. The custodians offer skills stored in their surviving records: choose the training you will carry into Karth Vault. Recover the dawnseeds and escape so the engine can be restored. Every return strains the equipment and leaves less of your memory intact. The people waiting above need a working future, even if the old cities can never be rebuilt.

Eldest of the Seven Fathers, wrought in secret by Aulë ere Elves or Men drew breath, laid sleeping under stone till Ilúvatar granted waking. First of Dwarves to wake beneath Gundabad's stars, he wandered lands no foot had marked. At Kheled-zâram he beheld a crown of seven stars upon the deep — promise of the halls he would carve in living rock; there he raised Khazad-dûm, its pillars sunk to the mountains' roots, its forges bright with craft. Deathless they named him, returning age upon age through his line; Durin, father of the stone-folk, whose Mirrormere vision kindled a kingdom outlasting the drowning of Beleriand.

Dravik was a deep mason whose workshop marks became the charter of a lasting city. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Mighty fëa aflame, brightest and proudest among Eldar craftsmen, yet fallen under shadow, whose hand wrought Silmarils kindled grief and war. His fierce oath forever binds sons to ruin, and echoes still unbroken beyond death, through fire and wrath, to the world's unmaking or renewal. Restless in Mandos, his spirit burns fierce, awaiting doomed fulfillment when the Jewels return or fade, and Arda's wounded beauty is restored; yet ever marred, his legacy wrought in flame and boundless sorrow; brightest of the Noldor, deepest fallen — Fëanor, Spirit of Fire, whose glory and whose ruin are one flame.

Caedren was a furnace architect who concealed a dangerous shortcut in the weather engine. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

He is Morgoth Bauglir, the Black Enemy of the World, mightiest and most terrible of all beings in Arda. Once he was Melkor, greatest of the Ainur, but his pride and malice have diminished him, and now he rages with everlasting wrath upon his dark throne. In his right hand he bears Grond, the Hammer of the Underworld, and upon his iron crown blaze the three Silmarils, searing his brow with a pain he can neither endure nor release. He is the source of all shadow in the world, and the father of dragons, orcs, and every corruption that plagues the Children of Ilúvatar.

Varkesh the Iron Regent sits within the stolen crown assembly. Three dawnseeds feed his command apparatus while the weather engine above falls silent. The construction hammer in his hand was never meant for this work.

Mighty fëa aflame, brightest and proudest among Eldar craftsmen, yet fallen under shadow, whose hand wrought Silmarils kindled grief and war. His fierce oath forever binds sons to ruin, and echoes still unbroken beyond death, through fire and wrath, to the world's unmaking or renewal. Restless in Mandos, his spirit burns fierce, awaiting doomed fulfillment when the Jewels return or fade, and Arda's wounded beauty is restored; yet ever marred, his legacy wrought in flame and boundless sorrow; brightest of the Noldor, deepest fallen — Fëanor

Dravik was a deep mason whose workshop marks became the charter of a lasting city. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

'His shining shield was scored with runes to ward all wounds and harm from him.' A shield of mithril, the true silver, its face bright as starlight and inscribed with runes of warding by the loremasters of the Havens of Sirion. The mithril was brought from Khazad-dum, traded westward by the Dwarves through Ered Luin. Its name means 'Warding Shield' in Sindarin. The runes are words of staying and protection drawn from the deep lore the Noldor brought out of the West. Eärendil bore it when he sailed in Vingilot to plead before the Valar.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Wardplate'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. Its influence hastens recovery.

Cautious lord of Finarfin's line, who took the crown of Nargothrond when Finrod perished in Sauron's pit, keeping faith with a mortal friend. He hoarded hidden strength and shrank from open war, warding the delved halls beneath the Narog's murmuring waters. Yet Túrin's pride and Glaurung's cunning unwove the veils of his secrecy; on Tumhalad's bloodied field he fell, his halls cast down, Finduilas dragged into the dark, the river running red beneath the dragon. Orodreth, careful guardian whose walls could not hold the doom.

Orsel was a cautious administrator charged with the survival of the lower basin. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Fairest daughter of twilight, song and star blended beneath woodland leaves, whose voice defied Morgoth himself, beauty challenging darkness eternal. Love binding mortal heart to immortal soul, weaving fate unforeseen, foreshadowing hope and sorrow entwined, the world's destiny reshaped. Brave in love, daring paths forbidden, setting aside her timeless grace, destined to fade willingly from Eldar's light, mortal fate chosen bravely, remembered ever as Tinúviel, brightest jewel in Arda's song, grief and joy entwined.

Nysara was a signal singer who learned to open maintenance doors with resonant tones. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

The silver crown of Nargothrond, worn by Finrod Felagund, mightiest of the sons of Finarfin, who gave his life in defence of Beren at Tol-in-Gaurhoth. When Gorthaur challenged him to a contest of songs in that dreadful place, Finrod sang of the light of Valinor and the glory of the Elder Days, and for a time his music held the dark lord's power at bay. He cast aside this crown when he swore his oath to Beren and went forth into Angband disguised. It remembers his defiant song and stirs the same courage in its bearer.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Tavren'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal.

King of grey twilight, tallest among Elves, ruling hidden Doriath fair; whose wisdom guarded realms beneath enchanted forests, untouched by time. Pride stirred by Silmaril's light, destiny darkened through treasure's lure, fate woven tight with mortal hearts and grief, binding Eldar to Edain. His realm doomed by jewel-craft and dwarven greed; shadows gather swift, yet memory of greatness endures, haunting woods once bright with song, foreshadowing ruin wrought by desire, grief deeper than twilight itself.

Arveth was a reedland magistrate who guarded the only road through the wetlands. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

The black spear of Melkor Morgoth, mightiest of the Ainur who fell, wielded in the hour when he and the great spider Ungoliant came in darkness to the heart of Valinor. With this weapon he struck the Two Trees of Yavanna - Telperion the White and Laurelin the Gold—and Ungoliant's venom poured into the wounds until all the light of the world was swallowed. The weapon still carries a sliver of that primal malice, and even to touch it is to feel the cold of the Unlight that once shrouded the land in darkness.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Varkesh'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. It helps the bearer resist being held. Its hungry work draws vitality from wounds. Its attacks carry venom.

Faithful mariner, storm-tossed survivor, bearer of Ulmo's whispered hope, last messenger of Gondolin's hidden splendor, guided by fate unseen. His weary eyes glimpsed future sorrow, guiding mortal hero toward doom, footsteps bound by destiny, yet courage kindled by unyielding resolve. Foreseeing city's fall yet guiding hero onward through shadows deepening, heart burdened yet steadfast, fulfilling purpose woven by Powers above, bearer of hope amid despair, witness to glory lost beneath waves of flame.
Delvek was a navigator who returned with news from the drowned harbors. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

This armour bears the weight of sorrow and treachery alike. It was worn by Gorlim, called the Unhappy, one of Barahir's outlaws in Dorthonion after the Dagor Bragollach had laid that land waste. When his beloved Eithel was taken from him, Gorthaur's servants promised her return if he would betray his lord. Driven beyond endurance, Gorlim revealed Barahir's hiding place - only to learn Eithel was already dead and the promise but a lie. He was slain, and this armour has been black with shame ever since.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Pavrek'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift.

Master smith hidden deep beneath mountains, legend among Naugrim lords, whose skilled hands taught crafts divine, shaping metal into destiny. Secrets wrought in darkness beneath earth, wisdom shining in shadows deep, his knowledge bound to lineage of smiths whose deeds echo through ages. Foreshadowing future splendor and ruin alike, marvels and treasures forged, his teachings carry whispers of power and peril yet hidden by time, remembered in halls of stone, his craft enduring beyond fall and flame.

Orvek was an old foundry tutor who tested each invention before praising it. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Brave huntsman, faithful captain of Thingol's guard beneath starlit woods, whose spear guarded borders of Doriath, steadfast amid darkness growing. Witness of grief and ruin, whose noble heart wept silent tears unshed, burdened by tragedies foreseen yet helplessly endured in shadowed hours. Doomed yet unwavering companion to mortal heroes, bonds forged in sorrow, foresight dimmed by loss yet eyes reflecting courage amid despair, destined to fall loyal, remembered in lament beneath darkening trees.
Torren was a patient ranger who watched the outer dikes. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Wise shipwright, silver-bearded master mariner dwelling by western shores; foresight guiding weary hearts toward hope amid tides of endless grief. His keen eyes witness sorrows deepening, ships departing into twilight; entrusted by fate to craft vessels bearing hidden stars and secret fire. He watches patiently as realms fall, bound to wait until grief departs, foreseeing final voyages across seas yet veiled by shadow and sorrow, keeper of hope unseen, guiding future kings unto shores yet unknown.
Marvek was a shipwright who repaired the last evacuation ferries. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Steadfast third son of Finarfin, keen-eyed warden of the northern marches, whose counsel bridged the sundered houses of Noldor and Sindar. He bore to Thingol's guarded halls the tidings of the exiles' coming, and named the kinslaying plainly where softer tongues would have veiled it. Beside Aegnor he held Dorthonion through the long years of siege; and when the Bragollach broke in fire upon the pines, he fell beside his brother. Angrod, true of word and blade, whose watch ended in flame and sorrow.
Tavrik was a second sentry who maintained the warning fires. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Petty dwarf, last remnant of forgotten people, dwelling hidden in shadows; heart bitter, sorrowful survivor of ancient wrongs beneath grey hills. Guardian of secrets bound to sorrow, foreshadowing betrayal and grief, his eyes dark with resentment, fate weaving tragedy for friend and foe. Deeds twisted by bitterness, vengeance awakening shadow unforeseen, destiny entwined tragically with mortals, ruin born from grudging heart, remembered with pity and dread alike, sorrow embodied in fading stones.
Kesket was an exiled mason who concealed supplies in forgotten shafts. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Fair-haired daughter of Finarfin, exile proud and wise beyond her years, eyes aglow with foresight, bearing grief of kin lost, kingdoms fallen. Dwelling now beneath twilight, silent watcher amid deepening shadows, feeling distant echoes of power yet to rise, and peril unforeseen. Her dreams foretell realms she shall shape, yet touched by subtle peril; rings of power yet unmade haunt visions, promising glory and grief alike, marking her path through sorrow and hope, unto fates unknown and mighty.

Yselle was a surveyor who mapped the tides when the old charts became useless. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Mortal hero, brave-hearted wanderer beneath stars, defying darkness, whose love challenged fate itself, winning Silmaril with courage unmatched. Destined to tread perilous paths, hand of shadow bound in silver fire, deeds woven in tragedy and triumph, uniting mortal and immortal blood. Foreshadowing line of hidden kings whose fate shall shape Arda's end, heart bound fiercely to Lúthien's grace, death conquered by timeless love, legacy ever shining, his story echoed eternally in stars and song.

Senvar was a courier who crossed occupied tide gates carrying a stolen route map. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

A shortbow crafted in Doriath by the hunters who served under Beleg Cuthalion, the greatest archer of the Sindar. Though unadorned, its wood was cut from the heart of a yew that grew within the Girdle of Melian, where the Queen's power quickened all living things. When drawn, the archer's eye is guided as if by the foresight of the Maia herself, finding the gaps in armour and the weakness in every defence. The hunters called it 'Death's Sting' for the way its arrows found their mark unerringly.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Death's Needlewake'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal.

Eldest son of fire-hearted Fëanor, whose flame-red hair now shadows grief; once chained in torment on cliffs of Thangorodrim, yet unbroken in spirit. Leading brothers in doom-bound quest, his nobility falters beneath oath sworn rashly in pride, binding him to deeds grievous and sorrowful. Kin-slaying waits upon his road, and at its end a tragic madness: a Silmaril seized again in flame and despair, and hope brought to its bitter ending; Maedhros the Tall, who gave his right hand for his life.

Rethan was a crane operator who survived a collapsed gantry and returned to duty. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

High King courageous, whose defiance shook Morgoth upon his dark throne; riding alone to Angband's gates, fearless, shining in wrathful valor. Though fallen, his horn still echoes through desolate wastes of the North, his broken sword and rent shield signs of undying pride and despair. His bravery inspires kin, yet foreshadows heavier losses still to come, until the darkness is pierced by brighter stars in days unforeseen. Fingolfin rests in Mandos, spirit brightened by sacrifice and glory.

Brennek was a breakwater captain who challenged the regent at the intake gates. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

A long tapering shield wrought of wood overlaid with plates of white metal, bearing the device of a swan's wing upon a field of deep blue. It was left in Turgon's abandoned halls of Vinyamar at the command of Ulmo, Lord of Waters, to await the messenger who would one day come to warn of Gondolin's doom. Tuor son of Huor found it upon the shore of Nevrast and bore it to the Hidden City. Untarnished by the long years of waiting, it lends its wearer endurance against the breaking of the heart.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the White Ferry'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift.

Mortal children, whose brief lives shine bravely amid shadows of Eldar; their hearts bound fiercely to freedom, defying doom and dark despair. Heroes born amid ruin, whose strength will challenge Morgoth's shadow, forging bonds of love and sorrow binding them forever to Elf-kind. Foreseen to rise and perish swiftly, leaving deeds remembered in song, carrying hope beyond death, their bloodline destined for hidden glory, their fate to inherit Arda's weary dominion beyond Eldar's fading hour.

The Tideborn rebuilt on exposed banks after the old cities broke. Their lives are brief beside the stored memoryprints of the engine, but their communities learn quickly and share what the next flood might take. They bring urgency and stubborn resolve into the vault.

Noble prince of Nargothrond, brave warrior shadowed by captivity and grief, whose courage shone brightly yet dimmed beneath darkness of Angband's halls. Bound by sorrow and loss, returning marred to city of hidden caves, foreshadowing tragic ruin, love overshadowed by quiet despair. Companion doomed yet steadfast, guiding Túrin's fate unknowingly toward doom, remembered in lament, bravery bright amid shadows of defeat; Gwindor, noble spirit enduring darkness, remembered beyond ruinous fall.

Elvren was a returning prisoner who remembered the occupied tunnels too well. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Brave-hearted prince, valiant son of Fingolfin, friend to mighty Maedhros; fearless rescuer who cut friend free from torment upon dread peaks. His valor brightens briefly as High King, yet fate cruelly casts him down on Anfauglith's blackened plain, where Morgoth's shadow conquers courage. But his deeds yet inspire hope, shining as stars above fading realms, friendship unbroken even in death, his spirit ever watching kin afar, awaiting the final healing of wounds made by sword and sorrow.
Lereth was a rescue climber who went back for stranded workers. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Flame-eyed fourth son of Finarfin, whose spirit matched the northern fires he warded upon Dorthonion's pine-clad heights, beside his brother Angrod. He bore a hidden wound — Andreth the wise, mortal, beloved, never claimed amid the doom he foresaw. When the Bragollach loosed its rivers of flame, he stood unyielding on the burning slopes, blazing till fire took both flesh and valour; Aegnor, fell fire, brightness too swiftly quenched, an ember glowing yet in the sorrowful songs of twilight.
Tavrek was a highland sentry who watched the furnace approaches. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Lord of hidden Gondolin, builder of white walls beneath encircling peaks; proud and secretive, whose city once stood fair against Morgoth's malice. Yet pride sealed doom, ignoring warnings whispered by Ulmo's waves, as fire consumed towers and hope alike beneath betrayal's cruel hand. Though fallen, his bloodline endures in Eärendil, whose distant star foreshadows redemption far beyond sorrowful ruin of his city's dreams, awaiting a brighter hour when shadows break and stars shine anew.

Darsen was a city planner who built shelters inside abandoned cooling towers. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Noble lord, golden-haired leader beloved among Edain's bravest houses, whose banner shone proudly upon battlefield, courage bright in darkness. Heart generous yet fierce, bound in friendship and honor with Eldar lords, destined to fall bravely, leaving legacy borne by blood of heroes. His line foreshadows valor undimmed, sorrow mingled with future glory, memory cherished in halls of Men and Elves, defying shadow's power; emblem of mortal bravery, whose blood shapes Arda's hidden fate.

Garven was a harbor commander who held a narrow causeway through the evacuation. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Proud white lady, sister of Turgon, restless beneath Gondolin's towers, adventurous heart seeking freedom, riding paths through peril and shadow. Her fate entwined tragically, choosing paths leading into darkness unseen, foreshadowing doom bound with dark Elf-lord beneath twilight forest. Yet mother to hero fated to defy evil, destiny woven in sorrow, remembered with mourning in hidden city, warning of perilous pride; Aredhel, whose restless courage led toward grief and hidden heroism.

Perya was a trail rider who valued open banks more than the safety of the enclosure. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Renowned smith of Nogrod, whose mighty hammer shaped legends in iron; hands crafting marvels bound to fateful deeds beyond dwarven halls. Maker of swords whose edge would cleave darkness and challenge fate itself, his forge echoed prophecy of heroism, tragedy, valor, and betrayal. Blade forged destined to wound Morgoth himself, bound to mortal hero, weapons wrought in secret, glory shadowed by fate unforeseen, remembered by dwarves and Elves alike, name carved deep in lore and stone.

Kavren was a master toolmaker who shared workshop secrets with every willing apprentice. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Dark-hearted smith dwelling deep beneath gloomy forest halls unseen, crafting meteoric iron into blades of peril and subtle enchantment. Secretive and proud, bound by jealousy, shadow hiding heart's desire, fate entwined tragically with Aredhel, foreshadowing ruin and loss. Father to son who shares dark destiny, weaving doom in hidden halls, remembered bitterly in dark tales whispered beneath forest twilight; Eöl, elf whose pride forged tragedy beneath shadowed leaves of Nan Elmoth.

Zavrek was a reclusive metalworker who invented dusksteel and guarded its process. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Mighty dwarven lord of Belegost, brave-hearted defender of stone halls, whose fierce courage challenged dragons beneath red fire and shadow. Armor clad in valor, battling boldly amid ruinous flames unleashed, foreshadowing heroism unmatched, fate bound fiercely to dragon's breath. Fell bravely beneath claws of Glaurung, yet blade pierced scale and pride, remembered forever in dwarven lament, honor etched deep in stone, symbol of courage beyond doom, defying darkness at battle's end.

King Vrannik was a mine captain who kept furnace beasts from the sleeping quarters. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Keen-eyed, crafty-handed son of Fëanor, nearest heir to his father's fire; a skilled smith, whose subtle tongue kindles division, pride, and betrayal. Father to Celebrimbor, who shall one day forge the perilous Rings of Power. His deeds shadowed by ambition, exile now stains his name; his cunning whispers ruin into fate, marring the friendships of the Eldar and weaving treachery unseen, till by treason the seeds of doom are sown; Curufin the Crafty, dark echo of his father's flame.

Veskir was a precision mechanic whose brilliant repairs sometimes served private schemes. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

A lamp wrought by Fëanor himself for his father Finwë, High King of the Noldor. Set with crystals that captured the mingled light of Laurelin and Telperion, it was among the treasures kept at Formenos during Fëanor's exile. When Morgoth came with Ungoliant, Finwë fell defending his son's hoard, but this lamp escaped the Unlight. Its radiance pierces shadow and frees the bearer from ensnaring bonds, and its holy light unravels even the darkest curses laid upon the works of the Enemy.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Odran'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It helps the bearer resist being held. It carries a steady light.

Mariner foretold by prophecy, born of Eldar and mortal blood entwined, destined to voyage oceans unseen, bearing hope amid endless night. Guided by stars, his ship shall challenge darkness beyond western seas, bound by fate to Silmaril's radiant flame, piercing shadows eternal. His quest foreshadows deliverance, heralding doom for Morgoth's reign, forever sailing skies, immortal star shining above world's grief; Eärendil, brightest hope, whose journey defines Arda's final destiny.

Teralis was a pilot who sought the custodians across the flooded service reaches. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Valiant Lord of Gondolin, whose silver sword sang beneath city's towers; captain beloved, noble guardian at the gates of secret splendor. His voice echoed brightly in fountain-filled squares, stern yet gentle, eyes keen with foresight of doom hidden beneath white walls of pride. Foreshadows heroism unmatched, battling shadow in ruinous hour; fate bound to duel dread lord of Balrogs, both falling in glorious flame, a legacy ever remembered in song beneath stars and shattered stone.

Cevran was a fountain engineer who fought to keep the emergency pumps running. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Proud lady of Dor-lómin, heart unbowed beneath shadows of despair, mother fierce yet silent, watching doom unfold upon kin and homeland. Strength hidden beneath grief, heart steadfast amid cruel darkness, foreshadowing tragic bravery, her line destined for shadow and flame. Her pride and sorrow shaping quietly fate of hero doomed by curse, remembered ever in tales of valor and grief entwined beyond mortal bounds; Morwen, proud heart enduring loss, courage veiled by sorrow unspoken.
Mardis was a shelter keeper who organized food and water under siege. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Dark-haired warrior, tragic son of doom, shadow-haunted mortal hero, whose blade, black and shining, cleaves fate amid relentless sorrow. Driven by pride and grief, defying Morgoth's curse yet bound within it, friend and foe entwined in tragic deeds, shadows deepening ever. Foreshadowing final despair, heroism tarnished by doom inevitable, yet courage undaunted, destined to slay dragon and darkness alike; memory forever mingled with glory and grief, Túrin Turambar—master of fate.

Drennar was a veteran whose choices in the furnace war left a trail of unpaid debts. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Noble-hearted builder of halls beneath Nargothrond's fair stone towers, friend steadfast and gentle, beloved of Men, faithful unto death itself. Sacrificed life to fulfill oaths made in love, honor, and courage, wrestling darkness for sake of mortal friend, forever remembered. Though fallen, his song yet echoes in lands where his kin wander, spirit bright in halls of Mandos, witnessing doom and destiny unfold—his deeds foretelling bonds of friendship bridging mortal and immortal.

Tavren was a choral technician who could tune a damaged control line by ear. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Wise-hearted and gentle, fairest prince who turned back from doom, ruling now in Valinor's quiet peace, sorrowful yet patient, waiting for the day when the bitter wounds dividing Noldor and Valar heal. His children's deeds across sea and time will bring honor and sorrow; yet in foresight he sees a distant hope, beyond ruin, grief, and loss, that blood shed by kin will one day lead to healing, renewal, reunion—and his heart longs for the far-off hour of redemption and forgiveness.
Osriel was a reservoir mediator who kept rival crews at one table. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Wise woman of Edain, keeper of lore and quiet wisdom deep and hidden, whose heart held love secret, bridging sorrow between Elf and mortal. Bearing hope dimmed by mortal fate, questioning destiny beyond grief, foreshadowing deeper mysteries of Men, mortality woven with hope. Her wisdom shapes quiet counsel, speaking truths gently to immortal ears, remembered softly in Eldar memory, her questions echoing unanswered; Andreth, mortal voice of sorrow and hope bound in tales unending.

Sevra was a tide scholar who studied the cost of life extended by the recall engine. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Golden-haired lord, valiant defender of Gondolin's doomed white towers; fierce guardian whose final battle cast Balrog down to fiery ruin. Fallen hero, whose sacrifice on mountain heights foreshadows rebirth, awaiting summons from Mandos, granted life anew by Valar's grace. Destined yet to return, bearing hope amid shadows of future darkness, protector whose bright spirit shall guide hidden paths of peril, until at last he rises again, ever watchful, a beacon of immortal valor.

Eralen was the former flood marshal of Aster Quay, recalled with gaps in the memory of the evacuation. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Strongbow of Doriath, brave-hearted ranger whose arrows sang in twilight, friend steadfast beyond measure, whose courage guarded realms in peril. Devoted companion to mortal friend, bound by love and tragic fate, foreshadowing betrayal unmeant, grief deeper than death itself. His noble heart foreseen pierced by friend's tragic blade in darkness, sorrowful fate sealed, yet deeds inspiring bravery even amid grief, forever honored as faithful guardian whose loyalty outshines doom.

Jassel was a watch captain who tracked missing crews through the reed beds. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Fair and wise, children of the gentle-hearted Finarfin, golden-haired, guided by wisdom rather than wrath, yet sharing kin's tragic exile. Builders of bright kingdoms soon to fall, guardians of ancient songs, whose deeds bind Elf to mortal Man, friendship shining through darkness. Bearing quiet grief amid glory, foreseeing ruin yet trusting hope, their line foretells redemption distant, beauty flowering from loss - bridging sorrowful exile and final healing in days yet unseen.

The Lantern Houses kept records, signals, and water agreements between the tide cities. Patient observation and clear thought are their inheritance. They seek a working future rather than the restoration of a vanished court.

Hardy smith-folk dwelling beneath mountains, masters of stone and metal, crafting marvels in deep halls, secretive yet fiercely loyal friends. Hearts bound to treasures glittering beneath earth, pride and greed entwined, foreshadowing conflicts bitter yet bravely fought against shadow. Their hands shall shape future splendor, halls both wondrous and doomed, forging swords and armor destined to echo peril yet unseen, allies steadfast and perilous, whose fate is carved in stone.

The Deep Masons built foundations and service ways under the tide cities. They value dependable tools, exact promises, and work that survives its maker. Their settlements endured below the floodline, paying dearly for every dry chamber.

Proud dwarven king, lord of wealth whose eyes darkened with greedy fire, driven by lust for Silmaril's beauty, weaving betrayal and doom. His heart foreshadows bitter conflict, dwarven honor stained by greed, hands grasping fate unmeant, binding destiny to ruin unforeseen. Doomed to fall, pride crumbling beneath shadows of treachery and wrath, legacy darkened by tragic ambition, forgotten by halls of gold, name whispered grimly, memory marred by deeds wrought in tragic pride.
Dromek was a tunnel guild ruler who protected the deep settlements. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

A massive glaive forged by the Dwarves of the Blue Mountains in the years before the rising of the Sun, when Morgoth's creatures first assailed their halls. Gaurin was a champion of those ancient Dwarves, and with this blade he broke through the walls of Rodrim's hall when orcs had sealed the gates. Its edge cleaves stone and steel alike, and it may yet be enchanted further by a skilled smith. '...the glaive of Gaurin whose gleaming stroke did rive the rocks of Rodrim's hall.'

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Dorran'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. Its edge bites through protection.

The grey cloak of Elu Thingol, tallest of all the Eldar and King of Doriath, who ruled beneath the enchantments of his queen Melian in the hidden realm of Menegroth. Before even the Sun rose, Thingol heard the music of Ulmo by the waters of Cuiviénen and was moved to a wonder none could match. How this cloak passed from Doriath into the wider world, none can say. It bears the silver-grey of the beech forests beneath the Girdle, and its folds ward against flame and frost alike.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Arveth'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. It guards against fire. It guards against cold. It helps the bearer resist being held.

Silver-footed princess of Gondolin, whose beauty shone brightly amid ruin, wise-hearted, foresight guiding hidden paths through doom and shadow. Love binding mortal and immortal hearts, shaping fate unforeseen, foreshadowing survival beyond flames, bearing hope anew amid despair. Mother of mariner destined to sail skies bearing hidden fire, her courage endures through darkness, quietly preparing future's light; Idril, bright star guiding destiny toward renewal beyond sorrow.

Sereth was a relief planner who prepared escape routes before the council believed the danger. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Grey-Elves, children of twilight, who lingered beneath starlit skies, wandering forests under shadows of Beleriand, guarded by secrecy. Melodious speech shaping beauty and sorrow into songs of twilight, suffering wars not of their making, hearts burdened by grief untold. Their doom bound to fading realms, yet resilience deep as roots of trees; amid ruin their wisdom blossoms quietly, awaiting renewal and peace beyond sorrowful days when forests burn and stars alone remember.

The Reedwalkers live where tide maps change each season. They read small movements in water and air, maintain hidden paths, and use songs to carry signals through the wetlands. Their knowledge reaches places city instruments cannot.

Twin sons youngest of fiery-hearted Fëanor, hunters beneath forest shade, sharing heart and fate alike, following brothers down paths of doom. Bound by father's Oath relentless, sorrowful deeds marked by grief, bearing flame-red hair symbolic of fire that consumes their house. Foreshadowing tragic end amid flames ignited by cursed desire, destined to perish in futile pursuit, kinship severed by treachery; memory fading like embers, names whispered sadly beneath starlit skies.

Kethren was a marsh hunter accustomed to fighting beside a trusted partner. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Greatest minstrel of twilight realm, singer whose melodies haunted woods, heart bound secretly in sorrowful longing, songs shaped by love unseen. His lament echoes through ages, voice weaving melancholy fate, driven to wander in grief, yet remembered by heartbroken Eldar. Foreshadowing exile and solitude, artistry born from sorrow unending, melodies forever entwined with shadow, beauty enduring amidst loss; Daeron, mournful voice whose music outlasts realms and time itself.
Lysven was an archivist who preserved the calibration songs. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Valiant chieftain of mortal Men, defender bold amid ruinous shadows, whose loyal heart defied Morgoth's wrath beneath northern darkness. Bearer of ring pledging friendship eternal between mortal and Elf-kind, fate bound by courage unyielding, guarding hope despite despair. His deeds foreshadow heroic legacy, bloodline destined for hidden glory, death faced nobly, yet memory survives beyond flames and sorrow; remembered ever as beacon of honor in night's relentless storm.

Havren was a militia captain who bound scattered settlements into a working defense. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

The dagger of Azaghal, Lord of Belegost, who stood against Glaurung the Father of Dragons in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad when all others fled. The Dwarves alone could withstand the dragon's gaze, and when Glaurung bore down upon Azaghal, the Dwarf-lord drove this blade into the dragon's belly—the first wound Glaurung ever suffered. Azaghal died crushed beneath the wyrm, but Glaurung fled in agony. The blade is still black with dragon-blood and burns with the wrath of Belegost.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Vrannik'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It guards against fire. Its edge bites through protection. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons.

These boots have been worn by more than one fugitive through the dread forest of Taur-nu-Fuin, where Morgoth's curse turned the fair woods of Dorthonion into a waste of shadow and malice, and the trees were bent to watch and betray. Beren passed through there on his long road to Nargothrond, driven near to madness by the whispers of the corrupted wood. These boots tread lightly upon rotting leaves, making no sound, and still carry some charm against the forest's spite.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Rust Orchard'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It aids quiet movement.

Dark-tempered fourth son of Fëanor, lord fierce of wide eastern lands, stern-hearted prince whose proud eyes burned beneath shadowed brows. Ruled wealth and trade, yet pride bred division with allies and kin, foreshadowing bitter conflict and wrathful deeds amid ruinous war. Destined to perish fiercely, falling bravely yet tragically, his spirit bound restlessly to father's oath, ever unfulfilled; Caranthir, proud lord whose wrath echoes beneath flame-shadowed skies.

Vordek was a quartermaster who hid private reserves behind a show of generosity. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

A pack of three perfectly balanced throwing spears, crafted in the secret forges of Gondolin. They bear the emblem of a swallow in flight, the sigil of the House of the Swallow, whose lord Duilin was the swiftest of all the Eldalie to run and leap. Known as 'Tuilindor' in the High Elven tongue, these weapons fly true as the birds they are named for. They sing of the valiant defense of the northern walls, where the Swallow-folk rained death upon the encroaching dark.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Swiftpins'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

Melodious second son of Fëanor, whose voice wove sorrow into song, bard-prince bound by oath, yet heart gentler than brothers proud. His harp whispered grief amid ruins, lamenting kin-slaying's shadow, foreshadowing lone wandering by restless shores beneath starlit waves. Hands destined to grasp Silmaril, burning guilt into weary heart, songs turning ever mournful, haunting waves until world's end; Maglor, tragic minstrel, forever bound to memory and bitter regret.
Sivren was a lament singer who kept the names of lost crews alive. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Mortal messenger chosen by Ulmo, guided by wave and whispered dream, bearer of hidden hope to Gondolin, destined to kindle fading valor. Heart bound in love with Eldar princess, bloodline uniting two worlds, foreshadowing renewal beyond ruin, fate entwined with Eldar's end. Bold protector in Gondolin's final flame, escaping shadow's grasp, father to mariner whose star heralds doom and deliverance alike; Tuor, mortal whose legacy shapes fate beyond sorrowful days.
Orren was a gate runner who brought warning from a sealed district. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Noble prince of twilight woods, wise lord whose heart bears hidden grief, destined guardian of fading realms beneath shadows yet unseen. Bound by love to Lady whose wisdom shapes fate of realms unknown, foreshadowing exile and sorrow mingled with enduring strength. Quietly guiding kin through darkness, steward of fading splendor, his fate woven subtly, surviving ruin and watching stars diminish; Celeborn, silent watcher, whose heart endures beyond sorrowful loss.
Talvek was a keeper of orchard stores who rationed the last living seeds. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Proud-hearted shieldmaiden, leader brave of forest-dwelling folk, steadfast in valor, defying darkness beneath shadowed woodland halls. Unyielding in courage, guiding people through peril and loss, spirit unbroken by sorrow, foreshadowing strength in days of despair. Her resolve shapes destiny of mortal hearts bound by fierce independence, remembered as flame undimmed, inspiring resilience amidst ruin; Haleth's name echoing proudly among tales of mortal defiance.
Jorva was a dike builder who refused to abandon a stranded community. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Star-bright heir of kings, child of Eldar bloodline noble and doomed, destined to bear crown amid shadows of ruinous First Age's end. Heart strong with wisdom and valor, guiding remnants toward distant shores, foreshadowing kingship beneath fading stars, yet untouched by flame. Courage enduring through darkness, leader born amid turmoil's grief, memory destined to shine even unto ages beyond ruin's shadow; Gil-galad, name whispered with hope amid Elven twilight.
Zereth was a young commander who inherited a fleet of damaged ferries. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Grandson of Fëanor, gifted smith with heart less marred by pride, whose hands shall shape hidden destinies forged in silver and gold. Dwelling now in youth's innocence, yet fate shadows every hammer-fall, foreshadowing glory and peril entwined in future rings of power. His deeds shall echo bitter legacy of kin, yet nobler in heart, shaping destinies far beyond mortal span, beauty marred by betrayal; remembered as greatest smith after Fëanor, tragic heir of craft.
Ferrik was a young craft leader who rebuilt tools from wreckage. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Mightiest mortal warrior, defiant heart opposing Morgoth's darkness, whose valor on Anfauglith echoed courage beyond mortal despair. Bound cruelly to doom, witnessing ruin wrought upon kin and realm alike, sorrow unmatched, yet spirit unbroken amid relentless torment. Foreshadowing tragic deeds borne of bitterness and wrathful grief, memory enduring in pride and tragedy, hero forever defiant; Húrin, steadfast flame, challenging darkness even unto bitterest end.

Vardek was a stubborn defender imprisoned for years beside the tide gauges. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Proud-hearted sons of flame, heirs bound eternally by their father's relentless Oath, pursuing stolen Jewels through ruin and despair. Noble in pride yet shadowed by deeds darkened by betrayal and grief; their swords ever turned against kin, blood staining their legacy. Driven to exile, oath-bound fate guiding their feet toward sorrow, foretold to fade in flame and ruin beneath desperate quest's end, leaving memory of greatness marred forever by tragic pride.

The Furnace Houses descend from crews who built the engine heart. Their gifts for craft and command survived the breach, as did the reckless covenants that divided their workshops. They return to the deep to recover what their work made possible.

Maia of divine grace, veiled in mortal form, guardian of twilight woods, whose enchantment shielded realms from Morgoth's shadow and despair. Love bound her heart to Elf-lord Thingol, fate entwined tragically, wisdom foreseeing sorrow yet helpless against destiny's tides. Her power foreshadowed protection's fall, woven spells unraveling, grief deepening as doom approached, yet beauty undiminished; Melian, heart both mighty and sorrowful, shaping fate subtly.

Meyra was a cloaking specialist who hid a settlement behind engine interference. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Valiant and steadfast people, following Fingolfin's bright banner through cold Helcaraxë's treacherous ice to realms darkened by war. Their courage tested against Morgoth's might beneath northern skies, enduring loss bravely, hearts unbowed even in bitterest defeat. Foreshadowing doom upon Anfauglith's fields, bravery unmatched, their legacy marked by noble defiance, sacrifice beyond despair, forever remembered as flames of valor beneath gathering shadow.

The Breakwater Houses grew from crews who held the sea gates. Their skill is tested under pressure, with no room to step aside. Memories of the failed evacuation give their courage a hard and costly edge.

Fierce-hearted third son of Fëanor, fiery hunter beneath wild woods, prideful prince whose noble beauty hid ambition and cunning deeds. Hunter whose hound's loyalty outshone his own heart's shadowed honor, foreshadowing betrayal born of lust for jewels and glory. Destiny stained by pursuit ruthless, turning kin against kin, marred forever by treachery against love and friendship sacred; Celegorm, proud hunter fallen, memory darkened by tragic desire.

Casken was a quarry hunter who could follow a footprint through falling ash. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

'...the knife of the north, in Nogrod smithied.' A keen-edged dagger forged by the smiths of Nogrod in the Blue Mountains, whose craft was renowned across all Beleriand. Its edge never dulls, proof of the art that produced Angrist and the Dragon-helm alike, and its blade is perfectly balanced for throwing. The Dwarves made it for trade along the great roads with the Sindar, though none who bore it are remembered in the songs of those days.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Frostspike'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work. Its edge bites through protection.

Forged from meteoric iron by Telchar of Nogrod, this dagger slices through iron as easily as flesh, earning its name: 'Iron Cleaver'. Curufin bore it until Beren wrested it from him. In Angband, while Morgoth slumbered under Lúthien's enchantment, Beren cut a Silmaril from the Iron Crown with this blade. When he reached for a second jewel, the knife snapped upon the crown and Morgoth stirred. Even broken, it remains peerless among daggers.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Locksplitter'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. Its exceptional edge cuts through armor.

A dark axe with a wicked and hungry edge, forged in the deepest pits of Angband by Morgoth Bauglir himself for the breaking of kin and the severing of hope. Many are the lives it has claimed, and each one it remembers: it is blood-warm to the touch and thirsting always for vitality, drinking deeply of those it wounds. Those who wield it are haunted by the cries of the slain—mothers weeping over fallen sons in the wars of Beleriand.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Lost Convoy'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. Its hungry work draws vitality from wounds.

This ring was wrought by Mairon in the earliest darkness of the First Age, when he still moved among the Valar feigning faithfulness to the light. Drawn to Melkor's mastery, he fled in secret to Angband and there, in forges where no light had fallen since the world was young, he shaped this band as a token of his allegiance. Shadows and Unlight cling to it, and to wear it is to feel the cold cunning of the Enemy's chief servant.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Sareth'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime. It reveals presences that evade ordinary sight. It aids quiet movement.

A great spear with a point like a sharp thorn of steel, originally forged by the Noldor for hunting the great spiders of Nan Dungortheb. Ogbar, a chieftain of the Easterlings who served Morgoth, slew its bearer in the treachery of the Nirnaeth Arnoediad and claimed it as spoil. Though made for nobler hands, the spear's virtue remains—its edge is death to the spawn of Ungoliant, and it pierces the thickest spider-hide with ease.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Varkun'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. Its edge bites through protection. It is a bane to spiders.

A bright mail corslet worn by Fingon the Valiant, who alone dared climb Thangorodrim to rescue Maedhros from Morgoth's torment. When he could not loose the iron band, Thorondor bore him aloft and he cut off his friend's hand to free him. Fingon became High King after Fingolfin fell, and wore this gilded mail until the Nirnaeth Arnoediad. It shines like the sun and fills the wearer with the courage that defied Morgoth's shadow.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Lereth'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening.

A great black helm wrought in Utumno, Morgoth's first fortress beneath the mountains of the uttermost North. For uncounted ages Utumno festered in darkness while Morgoth bred his terrible servants. When the Valar broke its gates, many treasures were lost in the ruin. This helm survived, bearing still the malice of those lightless depths. It grants strength and will, yet bends the wearer's purpose toward its first dark master.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Sunken Works'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It guards against cold.

Brutal gauntlets forged in Angband for the orc-chieftain Gorgdaz, who led Morgoth's host against the newly-arrived Noldor. He fell in the Dagor- nuin-Giliath, the Battle under Stars, when Fëanor's fury drove the orcs back to the very gates of Angband. The gauntlets are heavy with black iron and malice, crushing anything in their grasp, and they swallow light as if hungering for the darkness of the pits where they were forged.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Sumpcleaver'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched.

A great axe forged in Belegost, the northern Dwarven city of the Blue Mountains. Both blade and haft are made from a single piece of blackened steel. Engraved upon the axehead are the names of Belegost's valiant fallen—warriors who stood against Morgoth's trolls when they descended from Angband. It is called 'Mazarbulbark' in the Dwarven tongue, meaning 'the axe that is written upon', and it fills its wielder with vengeance.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Graven Oath'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. Its edge is especially dangerous to trolls.

A robe that belonged to Idril Celebrindal, the golden-haired princess of Gondolin and only child of King Turgon. She alone foresaw the city's doom and prepared the secret way of escape that saved the survivors. Celebrindal means 'Silverfoot', for she went barefoot even in the snows. The soft folds invigorate the wearer and fill the heart with thoughts of the swift eagles of Manwë, who watched over the Hidden City from afar.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Sereth'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It lends speed to its bearer.

Vallach was among the Balrogs who burst forth in the Dagor Bragollach, the Battle of Sudden Flame, when rivers of fire poured from Thangorodrim. He moves with terrifying speed, a huge shape cloaked in flame and shadow, his fiery axe cutting down all in his path before they can even raise their weapons in defense. There is something headlong in his wrath, as though it will one day bear him and a golden lord to a common doom.
Verrusk, cinder fiend of Sudden Flame has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

This blade was taken up by Galadriel, daughter of Finarfin and mightiest of the Noldorin women, when Fëanor's host turned upon the Teleri at Alqualondë to seize their white ships. She fought fiercely against the Kinslayers in defence of her mother's kin, yet the Doom of Mandos fell upon her nonetheless when she crossed the sea in pride, seeking a realm of her own to rule. The blade remembers both her valour and her sorrow.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Yselle'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift.

Boots that belonged to Finrod Felagund, King of Nargothrond and friend of Men, who gave his life defending Beren in the pits of Tol-in-Gaurhoth. Even in chains he fought a werewolf with his bare hands and slew it, though the battle cost him his life. These boots were made for riding in Valinor, but they grant their wearer nimbleness on any ground, letting them pass through battle as a dance and slip free of any binding.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Tavren'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It helps the bearer resist being held.

A long blade that glows with pale light, its hilt wrapped in red leather. When Ungoliant fled from Morgoth's Balrogs, she spawned many foul children in the Ered Gorgoroth, and their webs filled the dread valley of Nan Dungortheb. The Noldor forged this sword to cleanse those mountains, and many of her spawn fell to its edge. It wards against venom and darkness, a bane to all who crawled forth from that lightless brood.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Uzzara's Lament'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It helps resist venom. It helps the bearer resist being held. It carries a steady light. It is a bane to spiders.

Forged by Telchar of Nogrod, greatest of the Dwarf-smiths, this blade is called the sword of Sun and Moon, for Nar is the flame and Sil the silver light, and between them it burns with both. Its edge has known the blood of darkness and the warmth of starlight alike, wrought in the deep fires of the Blue Mountains with all of Telchar's art. Yet a greater fate is written upon it than any tale of the Elder Days may tell.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Daybreaker'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. It guards against fire. It guards against cold. Its edge bites through protection. It carries a steady light.

A corslet from the treasury of Durin the Deathless, eldest of the Seven Fathers of the Dwarves, who awoke beneath Mount Gundabad and founded Khazad-dum. He lived so long that he was called Deathless, and his folk believed his spirit would return in his heirs. This mail is wrought with the skill of the eldest days, proof against fire and frost, and it mends the hurts of battle as Durin's line endures through the ages.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Dravik'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It guards against fire. It guards against cold. Its influence hastens recovery.

At last before them far away they saw the glimmering wraith of day, the mighty archway of the gate - and there a horror new did wait. Upon the threshold, watchful, dire, his eyes new-kindled with dull fire, towered Carcharoth, a biding doom: his jaws were gaping like a tomb, his teeth were bare, his tongue aflame; aroused he watched that no one came, no flitting shade nor hunted shape, seeking from Angband to escape.
Ruzzak guards the last pressure gate. Its jaw has been reinforced with hot iron, and every escaping traveler must pass within reach.

Boots bearing the insignia of the House of the Mole, whose lord was Maeglin, son of Eol and Aredhel. He delved deep beneath Gondolin seeking metals and gems, and his miners discovered the foundations of the city. Yet Maeglin's heart was dark, and his love for Idril twisted into the betrayal that doomed the Hidden City. These boots are covered in dark moleskin, and their wearer moves silent as shadow through the deep.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Burrow Crew'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift.

The axe of Durin the Deathless, eldest of the Seven Fathers of the Dwarves, who awoke alone beneath Mount Gundabad and founded Khazad-dum. Its haft is carved with the symbols of all Seven Fathers. A sapphire in the blade glows softly in darkness, for Durin first beheld his reflection in the Mirrormere and saw a crown of stars above his head. The axe feels light in hand and bolsters the hearts of those who delve deep.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Dravik'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing. It is worked from lumesilver.

'His bow was made of dragon-horn.' A great bow fashioned from the horn of a slain dragon in the Havens of Sirion, where the remnants of Gondolin and Doriath gathered after those realms fell. Its name means 'Dragon-cleaver' in the tongue of the Sindar. The Eldar of Avernien blessed it with many enchantments against the terrors of the Enemy, and it wards the mind against fear and confusion, a last gift of a dying age.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Drakepiercer'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

The staff of doom borne by Turgon, King of Gondolin, when he sat upon his high throne to pronounce judgment. None could gainsay his decrees, for he was stern and proud as his father Fingolfin. With this staff he declared the fates of all who came before him, and even condemned Eol to death for the slaying of Aredhel. Its bearer commands the same dread majesty as the Hidden King who defied Morgoth until the very end.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Darsen'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched.

A sword forged in the secret forges of Gondolin, gleaming like a blade of winter ice when drawn. The Orcs knew it as the Goblin-cleaver and fled before its edge, for it was wrought to be their especial bane. It is the mate to Glamdring, the Foe-hammer, and when both blades are wielded together they sing in sharp accord, as they did in the Elder Days when the lords of Gondolin bore them against the hosts of Morgoth.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Breachfang'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work. Its edge is especially dangerous to orcs. Its edge is especially dangerous to trolls.

A ring of twinned serpents with emerald eyes meeting beneath a crown of golden flowers. Finrod Felagund gave it to Barahir after Barahir saved his life in the Dagor Bragollach, vowing eternal friendship between his house and Barahir's line. When Beren came to Nargothrond bearing this ring, Finrod honoured his oath even unto death. It is a token of the most faithful bond between Elves and Men in all the Elder Days.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Havren'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It helps resist venom. It helps the bearer resist being held.

A sleek hand axe forged by Maeglin, Lord of the House of the Mole, who learned his father Eol's secrets of working Galvorn and star-iron. The blade is dark as a moonless night and cuts through armour with ease. Maeglin delved deep beneath Gondolin seeking metals and gems, and his skill was great—yet he betrayed the Hidden City to Morgoth for the promise of Idril. This axe remembers that treachery in its very edge.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Ossresar'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. Its edge bites through protection.

'Of adamant his helmet tall, an eagle-plume upon his crest.' A great helm wrought of adamant, so hard that no blade could mar its surface. Upon its crest rises a plume fashioned in the likeness of an eagle's wing, in honour of Thorondor, King of Eagles, who aided the Noldor and the Edain against Morgoth. When Eärendil wore it upon the deck of Vingilot, the servants of the Enemy quailed before its terrible visage.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Skycrest'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing.

A cruel and heavy blade, wreathed in undying flames that burn without consuming. It was forged in the deepest pits of Angband for Gothmog, Lord of Balrogs and High Captain of Morgoth's hosts. With this sword he enforced the Dark Lord's will among the orc-hosts, and none dared defy him. The flames that wreathe it are of the same fire that burns within the Valaraukar themselves, cold-killing and terrible to behold.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Kilnrazor'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work. It carries a steady light. Its attacks carry flame.

A rune-etched knife of Mim, last of the Petty-dwarves who dwelt on Amon Rudh. His folk were the first Dwarves to enter Beleriand, exiled by their own kin, and they hated all others. When Túrin sheltered with him, Mim betrayed him to Morgoth's orcs for gold. The runes upon this blade exude venom, and a curse clings to it still—the bitterness of a diminished people and the treachery that brought their line to ruin.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Kesket'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It aids quiet movement. Its attacks carry venom.

The Hammer of the Underworld, forged by Morgoth himself in the depths of Angband and wielded in his duel against Fingolfin before the gates of his fortress. Thrice it smote the earth like thunder, making great pits into which the High King stumbled, and at last Morgoth set his foot upon Fingolfin's neck and broke him. It is blackened by dark sorceries, and its wielder commands the fear of all Morgoth's servants.
Ruinmaul was built to drive piles through the bedrock of the tide cities. Varkesh converted that engine tool into a weapon; each impact carries the force once used to anchor a seawall.

'Of silver was his habergeon.' A corslet of mithril chain, the true silver of the Eldar, light and supple as water yet proof against any edge. Its rings shine like stars upon the sea, and the Eldar of Avernien named it 'Gilceleb', Star-silver. It was part of the panoply of ancient kings that Eärendil donned when he armed himself for his great voyage, bearing the craft of both Gondolin and Doriath in its making.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Beaconmail'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime. It helps the bearer resist being held.

A cruel spear, black-hafted with a head of dark bronze, forged by Gorthaur in the years after the Dagor Bragollach when he walked openly through Beleriand spreading despair among Men. Sauron poured much of his own malice into its making, for he was a Maia in his own right, and the weapon bites through flesh and spirit alike without distinction. It throws no shadow, for darkness was bound into it at its forging.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Voidprong'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It helps the bearer resist being held. It reveals presences that evade ordinary sight. Its presence draws hostile attention. It is a bane to cinder fiends.

A mighty Dwarven mattock forged by Gamil Zirak, master smith of Nogrod and teacher of Telchar. Its name in Khuzdul means 'Axe-lord', for it was made for a king of Nogrod in the early days. Enchanted for both battle and mine, its heavy head crushes rock and skull with equal ease, and it can hew through stone as though it were rotten wood. Many are the tunnels delved by this tool, and many the foes it has broken.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Kingspick'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact.

A curved blade whose name means 'Blood-cutlass' in Sindarin, for its steel is stained the colour of old blood that no cleaning can remove. Some say it was forged by a Noldor smith driven mad by the Doom of Mandos, who quenched the blade in the blood of his own kin. It drinks deeply of those it wounds, sustaining its wielder even as it wakes a terrible hunger within them and clouds their mind with red thoughts.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Thirstcurve'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing. Its hungry work draws vitality from wounds.

A tall longbow painted in many bright hues, crafted by the House of the Heavenly Arch whose lord was Egalmoth. His folk loved colour and light, and their gear shone with gems and bright enamels. When Gondolin fell, Egalmoth led the rearguard through the Cristhorn with Glorfindel, and many orcs fell to their bows. This weapon draws smooth and true, the aim steady, and each shot flies where a deft will sends it.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Upper Aqueduct'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It carries a steady light.

This exquisite corslet was wrought in Gondolin by smiths who worked mithril brought from Valinor. Its rings are almost too small to see, yet each holds an echo of the stars Varda kindled before the awakening of the Elves. The Sindar called those stars 'the Swordsmen of the Sky', for they blazed forth to strike fear into Morgoth's heart. When darkness presses close, this mail gleams with their remembered light.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Beaconlace'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps.

'His sword of steel was valiant.' A keen-edged longsword from the Havens of Sirion, whose name means 'Foam-cleaver' in the tongue of the Sindar. When Eärendil armed himself for the great voyage, this was the blade girded at his side. It sheds a faint light and grows eager in the hand when the shadow of dragons falls near, as though it remembers the ruin of Ancalagon the Black above the towers of Thangorodrim.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Foamrazor'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons.

A sharp and well-made axe gifted to Haldan, Lord of the Men of Brethil, by the Dwarves of the Blue Mountains. When he asked its name, the Dwarves replied 'Binahkram'—meaning 'without name' in their secret tongue, for they do not share true names with outsiders. The Haladin, not understanding, took this as the axe's name, and so it has been called ever since. It bites deep into orc-flesh and spider-hide alike.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Seamrender'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime. Its edge is especially dangerous to orcs. It is a bane to spiders.

The fur-lined gauntlets of Bregolas, Lord of Ladros in Dorthonion and elder brother of Barahir, who would father Beren One-hand. When rivers of fire poured from Thangorodrim in the Dagor Bragollach, Bregolas fought shoulder to shoulder with Angrod and Aegnor until all three fell together. His line passed to Barahir, and thence to Beren. These gauntlets ward against the bitter cold of Dorthonion's high places.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Garran'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It guards against cold.

A small iron shield inscribed with spiralling runes that wind inward to a central spike. Its name means 'Shield-curse' in Sindarin, for it was wrought by the loremasters of Doriath to turn aside the dark sorceries of Morgoth's servants. The runes are words of unbinding and freedom, and the spike was made to pierce enchanted armour. With this shield, one may break the chains that the Enemy lays upon the will.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Spellstop'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing.

A sword forged in Vinyamar during Turgon's dwelling in Nevrast, before he departed to build Gondolin. Its name means 'Blue-sword' in Sindarin, for its blade has the grey-blue colour of the sea beneath clouds, and its hilt is white as foam. The cold winds of Nevrast are bound within it, warding off frost and holding the bearer free from snaring spells. It strikes swift and true as the sea-birds of that coast.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Bluewake'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. It guards against cold. It helps the bearer resist being held.

The helm left by Turgon in his abandoned halls of Vinyamar, at the command of Ulmo Lord of Waters, for the messenger who would one day come to warn of Gondolin's doom. Tuor son of Huor found it there, crowned with three swan's feathers, and wore it when he came at last to the Hidden City. It greatens the heart and clarifies the purpose of the one who wears it, for it was touched by the will of Ulmo himself.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Empty Docks'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

Greaves forged for Orodreth, who became King of Nargothrond after Finrod Felagund perished in Tol-in-Gaurhoth. Túrin's counsel led his realm to ruin, and Orodreth fell in the Battle of Tumhalad when Glaurung came against his host. These greaves were made to ward against dragonfire, though they could not save their bearer from the doom that the Father of Dragons brought upon the Hidden Kingdom of the Narog.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Orsel'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It guards against fire.

The spear of Gil-galad, last High King of the Noldor in Middle-earth, whose name means 'Snow-point' for its blade gleams white and is cold as ice to the touch. Gil-galad was young when Gondolin fell, but he grew to lead the remnants of his people at the Havens of Sirion. None could withstand Aeglos, and the servants of the Enemy fled before it, for its chill brings death to the undead and all fell spirits.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Rimespear'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It is a bane to the restless dead. Its attacks carry bitter cold.

A jewel once woven into the silver embroideries of Miriel Therinde, first wife of Finwë and mother of Fëanor.
