Serinde, the Broideress, she was called, for none could match her skill with needle and thread. So greatly did she spend herself in bearing Fëanor that her spirit departed to Mandos, never to return. This gem still holds the warmth of her hands and the light of the Trees under which she laboured.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Veira'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It carries a steady light.

A legendary blade of mithril, sung of in the ancient lays of Valinor. Its curved edge crackles with lightning, and in battle it moves swift as the storm-wind. Few have wielded it since the Noldor came to Middle-earth, for such a weapon demands a hand of great skill. '...the sweeping sickle of the slashing tempest, the lambent lightning's leaping falchion, even Celeg Aithorn that shall cleave the world.'

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Stormreaper'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing. Its edge bites through protection. Its attacks carry lightning.

Greaves forged by the host of Fingolfin during the dreadful crossing of the Helcaraxe, the Grinding Ice between Araman and Middle-earth. When Fëanor burned the ships at Losgar and abandoned them, Fingolfin's people walked the ice rather than return in shame. Many perished in that crossing, but those who survived became hardened beyond breaking. These greaves carry the endurance of that terrible journey.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the the Glass Strait'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It guards against cold. Its influence hastens recovery.

The weapon of Fingolfin, High King of the Noldor, who rode alone to Angband and challenged Morgoth to single combat. Seven times Ringil bit deep into the Dark Lord's flesh. Even as Morgoth crushed him, Fingolfin's last stroke hewed the foot of the Enemy, and Morgoth went halt ever after. The blade shines like a column of ice lit by light unquenchable, and its bitter cold burns the servants of darkness.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Rimewake'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It carries a steady light. Its attacks carry bitter cold.

These gloves bear the insignia of the House of the Swallow, whose lord Duilin was the swiftest of all the Eldar. His folk were famed as the greatest archers of Gondolin, raining death upon Morgoth's hosts from the northern walls. Duilin fell in their defence, struck by dragonfire even as he loosed arrow after arrow into the foe. These gloves steady the archer's hands and guide each shaft to its mark.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Swift Ferry'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps.

Son of Eol the Dark Elf and Aredhel of Gondolin, Maeglin rose high in the counsels of King Turgon. Yet his heart was consumed by forbidden desire for Idril Celebrindal, and when captured by Morgoth, he revealed the hidden location of Gondolin in exchange for promises of power and Idril as his bride. His treachery doomed the fairest of elven cities. The darkness in his heart has only deepened since.
Ossresar, Betrayer of Aster Quay has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

The greatest pearl ever found in the waters of Balar, given by Thingol to the Lord of Belegost as payment for the Dwarves' labour in delving Menegroth, the Thousand Caves. Its sheen is as starlight on the foam of the sea, and the Dwarves treasured it above all gems of their hoard. To hold it is to feel the peace of the shores of Balar before the wars came, when the Falathrim sang beneath the stars.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Tidepearl'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

The crown of Fëanor, greatest of the Noldor. It is beautifully wrought with many shining jewels of Valinor, whose light is a challenge to those born of darkness. Though his flaws ran deep, this crown is a reminder of his greatness, and of the terrible Oath that binds his sons to darkness. "Dear-bought those songs shall be accounted, and yet shall be well-bought.  For the price could be no other."

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Caedren'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It guards against fire. It reveals presences that evade ordinary sight. It carries a steady light. Its presence draws hostile attention.

The sister-blade to Anglachel, forged by Eol the Dark Elf in Nan Elmoth from the iron heart of a fallen star. Eol kept Anguirel for himself while giving Anglachel to Thingol as payment for dwelling in his realm. When Eol pursued his fleeing wife and son to Gondolin, his son Maeglin stole this sword and bore it ever after. A bitter blade by brooding Eol forged, in secret made of metal from a star.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Nightspindle'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It attracts danger. It aids quiet movement.

The twin of Amrod, keen-eyed tracker and hunter, sharing one heart and one fate with his brother; his loyalty bound not only to his twin but to the inescapable Oath sworn in pride and shadow. Foreshadowing a destiny mirrored in loss, his path tracks sorrow through the wilderness; his hunt ends not in glory, but in the tragic fulfillment of the curse, a life extinguished by the doom of the Noldor.

Kethra was a second marsh hunter whose timing complements a partner perfectly. In Karth Vault, the skills of that former life may help recover the dawnseeds. The decisions made along the way remain yours.

Lo! the golden dragon of the God of Hell, Father of Dragons, first of the Uruloki to issue from Angband. Glaurung led the assault in the Dagor Bragollach and wrought ruin upon Nargothrond. His gaze can bind the will and cloud the memory, and through such dark arts he brought doom upon Túrin Turambar and fair Niënor. His malice is matched only by his cunning, and his hoard is vast beyond measure.
Drazhul watches with the patience of a broken gauge. Its voice repeats facts you remember incorrectly until uncertainty gives way to obedience. Fire waits behind that quiet mouth.

'His arrows shorn of ebony.' Arrows fashioned from the heartwood of ebony, black and heavy, shorn to a keen edge and fletched with dark feathers. The Eldar of the Havens called them 'Mornpilin', the Dark Arrows. They were crafted for the dragon-horn bow and fly far and true against the winged terrors of Morgoth. In the War of Wrath, such shafts brought ruin upon the dragon-host above Beleriand.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Blackshafts'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. Its edge bites through protection. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons.

The iron spear of Boldog, a name borne by the mightiest orc-captains of Angband. Some say 'Boldog' was a title given to fell spirits who took orc-shape to lead Morgoth's hosts. This one led raids against the marches of Doriath, hunting for Lúthien at his master's command. The spear is heavy and brutal, forged in the dark pits, and wolves flee before it remembering their dread captain's wrath.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Zharrek'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It is a bane to wolves.

Gloves worn by Celebrimbor, son of Curufin and grandson of Fëanor, who inherited his forefather's skill at the forge yet rejected the Oath that cursed his house. In Nargothrond he crafted wonders of silver and gem, and he alone of his kin fought for Finrod against his own father and uncle. His greatest works still lie in the future, but these gloves grant steady hands for the finest craft.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Ferrik'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact.

The staff of Halmir, chieftain of the Haladin who dwelt in the Forest of Brethil. When the hosts of Morgoth marched south in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad, Halmir gathered his people and led them to war, though he was old. He died ere the battle, but his son Haldir fought in his stead, and the Haladin held their ground when all else fled. This staff embodies his steadfast will against the Shadow.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Jorreth'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing. It helps resist venom.

The sword of Elu Thingol, High King of the Sindar, whose name means 'King's Ire' in the tongue of his people. For three ages of starlight Thingol ruled in Doriath, and this blade was with him when he led the Sindar against Morgoth's orcs. Its jeweled hilt fills the bearer with the pride and will of that ancient king, though such confidence may draw peril as surely as it wards off fear.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Regent's Answer'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime. It attracts danger.

The shining mail of Finwë, first High King of the Noldor, wrought in Valinor before the Darkening. When Morgoth came to Formenos with Ungoliant, Finwë alone stood against him and was slain—the first of the Eldar to die in Aman. The Dark Lord took this corslet along with the Silmarils. It still gleams with the light of the Blessed Realm, untouched by the Shadow that claimed its bearer.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Odran'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise.

Gauntlets wrought of mithril by the jewel-smiths of Gondolin, who alone in Beleriand worked that precious metal brought from Valinor. Mithril was harder than steel yet could be beaten thin as silk, and these gauntlets are proof of that art. They protect the hands while granting them the deftness needed for the finest jewel-craft, as if the wearer's fingers were made of living silver.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Brightgrip'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal.

Heavy greaves forged for Caranthir the Dark in Thargelion, the harshest and most quick-tempered of Fëanor's sons. His face burned red with fury at the Mereth Aderthad when he nearly came to blows with the sons of Finarfin, and his wrath only grew through the long wars. These iron-shod greaves are made for charging headlong into the enemy, and they carry something of his furious heat.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Vordek'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work. It guards against fire.

The armour of Beor the Old, father of the First House of the Edain and first of Men to meet the Elves. Finrod Felagund found him singing by a waterfall in Ossiriand and became his friend. Beor served Finrod until his death, and his house remained faithful ever after. Though worn and simple, this armour was lovingly cared for, and it gladdens the heart in the dark places of the world.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Dovren'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work. It helps resist venom.

A shadowy cloak bestowed by Ulmo, Lord of Waters, upon Tuor at Vinyamar's shore when the Vala rose from the sea in storm and majesty. Ulmo alone among the Valar still watched over the exiled Elves and the Edain, and he sent Tuor to warn Turgon of Gondolin's doom. This cloak flows like deep currents, hiding the wearer from searching eyes and warding against the cold of deep places.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Ossan'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It guards against cold. It helps the bearer resist being held. It aids quiet movement.

Armour wrought of Galvorn, a metal devised by Eol the Dark Elf in Nan Elmoth. Black and shining as jet, yet hard as Dwarf-steel, Galvorn could be beaten thin and supple and still turn any blade. Eol made this suit for his son Maeglin, who wore it when he came to Gondolin. It carries echoes of the shadows of Nan Elmoth and of the treachery that would one day doom the Hidden City.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Ossresar'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing. It helps resist venom.

The Iron Crown of Morgoth Bauglir, in which burn the three Silmarils - jewels of Fëanor, stolen from Formenos and set here by the Dark Lord himself. In them burns the imperishable light of the Two Trees of Valinor, and the Oath of Fëanor compels his sons to claim them, even unto the ruin of the world. To cut a Silmaril from the crown, stand over it and use it (u), or press (k).
The regent's crown assembly is a brutal housing for the stolen dawnseeds. Its fastenings keep the power cells close to their captor while the tide cities wait for a working weather cycle.

A green jewel made by Enerdhil the smith in Gondolin, filled with the light of the Sun. Those who look through it see withered things as young once more, and the hands of one who wears it bring healing. Idril gave it to her son Eärendil, and through him it passed out of the Elder Days. It is called 'Elessar', the Elfstone, and great destiny lies upon it in ages yet to come.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Verdant Lens'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. Its influence hastens recovery.

A helm wrought of grey metal and set with the bones of an orc who dared raise his blade against his own master. In Angband, such treachery was punished with torments beyond imagining, yet this one's defiance was preserved in mockery. The helm carries the stain of betrayal, but also the power to break bonds—even the dread Oath of Fëanor holds less sway over one who wears it.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Broken Compact'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal.

Forged beneath Mount Dolmed by Gamil Zirak, master of Telchar and greatest smith of Nogrod in his time. The Dwarven road from Nogrod to Belegost ran through that mountain's pass, and this axe guarded it against Morgoth's servants for many years. It is an heirloom of Nogrod, granting strength to lift its great weight and fire in the blood to face the Balrogs and their kin.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Seam Ridge'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It guards against fire. It is a bane to cinder fiends.

Some have called the Balrogs 'Demons of Terror', but none inspires such dread as Delthaur. His very presence fills the heart with nameless fear, and the bravest warriors have fled screaming at his approach. Yet his malice turns most keenly against those who delve in the deep places of the earth, and dark halls may one day remember him by a darker title: the Bane of Durin.

Cindrek, cinder fiend of Terror has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety. Its presence can break courage.

The shield of Glorfindel, Lord of the House of the Golden Flower in Gondolin. When the Hidden City fell, he led the survivors through the mountains and faced a Balrog in single combat upon a narrow ledge. He slew the demon but fell with it into the abyss. His sacrifice ensured Tuor and Idril's escape, and legend tells that he was re-embodied by the Valar for his valour.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Eralen'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime.

The great hammer of Telchar of Nogrod, mightiest of all Dwarven smiths. With this hammer he forged Angrist the iron-cleaver, Narsil the sword of kings, and the Dragon-helm of Dor-lomin. Its hard steel has rung upon forge and anvil in the making of legendary works, yet it served equally well upon orc-shields when Morgoth's hosts descended upon the halls of the Dwarves.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Kavren'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It guards against fire.

The hunting blade of Amrod, youngest son of Fëanor along with his twin Amras. In Valinor, the brothers hunted with Oromë and Celegorm beneath the light of the Trees. Of all Fëanor's sons, they were the least eager for the Oath, yet they followed their father into exile. This blade carries the skill of those hunts, sharpening the senses and silencing the hunter's step.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Kethren'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It aids quiet movement.

The blade of Nan, a giant who dwelt in the frozen wastes north of Angband in the years before the rising of the Sun. Such creatures served Morgoth in those dark times, though they were few and wild. This sword is massive beyond mortal scale, yet one of great strength may wield it. When swung, it cleaves through armour and bone alike, impaling foes upon its length.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Pillarcleft'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise.

A black shield with scalloped edges, bearing the emblem of a white hand dripping blood. Such was the sign of certain orc-captains who swore blood-oaths to Morgoth, marking their hands in token of lives they would take. The shield grants fell strength to its bearer, but treachery clings to it, for those who bore this sign thought nothing of betraying their own.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Red Gauntlet'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact.

A hideous spirit out of the outer darkness, walking now in the form of a spider of monstrous size. A cloud of Unlight hangs about her, for she drinks every light that lives into her bloated body and weaves it forth again as choking dark. Her hunger has neither bottom nor end, and it is said that in her uttermost famine she will devour even herself at the last.
Uzzara spins insulation stolen from the engine cables into a choking web. It drains light from every live contact it reaches, swelling as the chamber goes dark.

Crafted for Aegnor, fourth son of Finarfin, who with his brother Angrod held the highlands of Dorthonion against Morgoth's hosts. He loved the mortal woman Andreth, yet refused to wed her lest war take him and leave her widowed. He fell in the fires of the Dagor Bragollach, and his love remained forever unfulfilled. This armour lends his fierce determination.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Tavrek'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps.

A bright long-knife of Gondolin, forged in the days when that hidden city still stood in glory. Its cold light kindles at the nearness of orc-kind, and its keen point is a bane to great spiders and crawling terrors. Though little is spoken of this blade in the songs of Beleriand, strange fate is woven about it, and it will yet play a part in tales unwritten.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Needlewake'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It helps resist venom. It helps the bearer resist being held. Its edge is especially dangerous to orcs. It is a bane to spiders.

A great helm of Dwarvish make, wrought deep in Khazad-dum with curving horns of black iron and a face-guard hammered into a stern and defiant visage. The Dwarves of Durin's folk crafted such masks in the deeps, for they were pride-stiff even when the darkness pressed close. When the hosts of Angband marched south, the Dwarves donned such helms and none fled.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the the Underfoundry'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It is worked from lumesilver.

The helm of Angrod, third son of Finarfin and brother of Finrod, Aegnor, and Galadriel. With Aegnor he held the highlands of Dorthonion against Morgoth's hosts for centuries, until both brothers fell in the fires of the Dagor Bragollach. This helm remembers the bitter winds of those high places and the courage needed to face the terror of Morgoth's flames.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Tavrik'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It guards against cold. Its influence hastens recovery.

A blade of black obsidian set in a hilt of twisted thorn-wood, perhaps fashioned by the Petty-dwarves in the years of their exile, or by some darker hand. The stone is slick with venom that never dries, and blood spilled upon it vanishes as though drunk by the wood itself. Those who bear it grow pale and hungry, yet find their footsteps grow ever lighter.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Briarsplint'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. Its hungry work draws vitality from wounds. It aids quiet movement. Its attacks carry venom.

A greatsword borne by Saithnar, an Elf-lord of the host of Fingolfin who fell fighting the houseless spirits and revenants that Morgoth sent forth from Angband. Its silver runes blaze against the undead, but the spirits of those Saithnar slew cling to the blade still, haunting its wielder with visions of ancient battles and the faces of the restless dead.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Velkar'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It reveals presences that evade ordinary sight. Its edge bites through protection. It is a bane to the restless dead.

A longbow of Sindarin craft, its name meaning 'Bent-wood' in that tongue. The Sindar of Doriath were great hunters and archers, and this bow was made by their bowyers for the wardens of the marches. Though worn at the notches from years of faithful service, it remains supple and true. Its arrows fly straight and swift, unhindered by enchantment or shadow.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Boughringer'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It helps the bearer resist being held.

The hunting blade of Amras, twin brother of Amrod. Like his brother, he  rejoiced in the hunt, riding often with Celegorm in the woods of  Valinor. Though bound by the terrible Oath, he dwelt long in the wild  lands of East Beleriand, far from the wars of Angband. This blade grants  the mastery of two weapons, striking with the swift accord of the twins.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Kethra'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It aids quiet movement.

A cloak worn by Maglor, second son of Fëanor and mightiest singer of the Noldor. Though bound by the Oath, he was the gentlest of his brothers and fostered Elrond and Elros after the sack of Sirion. When at last he held a Silmaril, it burned his hand, and he cast it into the sea. He wanders the shores still, and his songs of sorrow echo in this garment.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Sivren'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal.

A mantled shape of void that was once perhaps man or elf, now twisted beyond recognition by the necromancy of Gorthaur, greatest of Morgoth's servants. Noseless it scents the air, turning this way and that, drawn to the warmth of the living. Its touch brings a darkness that seeps into the very soul, and its will can hold a victim helpless as the grave.

This wraith has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It can pin a victim in place.

A cruel curved blade of black iron, forged in the pits of Orodruth in the years when Morgoth's power was unchallenged and the Elves yet slumbered by Cuiviénen. It is famed among the orcs as a slayer of Elves and Men, and chieftains have fought and murdered for the right to bear it. Its edge drains the wielder's spirit even as it grants fell strength.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Vexedge'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime. Its presence draws hostile attention.

The Iron Crown of Morgoth Bauglir, wrought in Angband to hold the stolen light of the world. Two sockets are empty and dark, but in the third burns still a Silmaril—a jewel of Fëanor, containing the imperishable light of the Two Trees of Valinor. It is the greatest treasure remaining in Middle-earth, and the Oath of Fëanor binds his sons to claim it.
The regent's crown assembly is a brutal housing for the stolen dawnseeds. Its fastenings keep the power cells close to their captor while the tide cities wait for a working weather cycle.

The iron gauntlets of Caranthir the Dark, Lord of Thargelion, whose fiery temper was feared even among his own brothers. He grew rich from trade with the Dwarves of the Blue Mountains, yet his hands were made for war more than counting treasure. These gauntlets are crude but fearsome, and they burn with the heat of their master's unquenchable wrath.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Vordek'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. It guards against fire.

Second only to Gothmog among the Valaraukar, Lungorthin commands the guard of Angband itself. His massive form is cloaked in flame so intense that the very stone beneath his feet is scorched black. His smouldering eyes have witnessed the fall of countless heroes, and his fiery breath has consumed armies. Few have faced him and lived to speak of it.

Kharvek, Lord of cinder fiends has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat.

Gloves that once belonged to Rumil, lore-master of Tirion in Valinor, who first devised letters and writing among the Elves. Before even Fëanor perfected the Tengwar, Rumil created the Sarati to record the words and wisdom of the Eldar. These gloves guided his hand in that delicate work, lending precision and subtlety to the wearer's every motion.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Esvik'. The regent sealed it away after confiscating the independent guild stores. Old custodians can recognize the workmanship through the grime.

Sire of all werewolves, Draugluin was bred by Morgoth in the pits of Angband and given to Sauron as captain of his wolf-hosts. Upon the Isle of Werewolves he dwelt, greatest and most terrible of his kind, until Huan of Valinor overthrew him. Yet death could not hold him long in the service of the Dark Lord, and now he stalks these halls once more.
Grozhak, Sire of Werewolves has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

Dagorhir towers above even the mightiest of trolls, clad in iron plates forged in the smithies of Angband. He earned the name Elfbane in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad, where his great hammer crushed countless sons of the Eldar. Now he leads patrols of the feared Troll Guard through the deep halls, and the sound of his tread brings dread to all who hear.
Drazken, the Elfbane has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

Greatest of Morgoth's servants, Gorthaur the Cruel was once a Maia of Aulë before he was seduced by Melkor's power. Master of werewolves and lord of Tol-in-Gaurhoth, he is a sorcerer of terrible might. He takes many forms, and now appears as a great wolf, the mightiest of his kind save only Draugluin. His eyes burn with malice older than the Sun.
Sareth trained the kennel packs and copied their shape into his altered body. Beneath the wolf hide is a precise and practiced cruelty.

Grizzled and cunning, Umuiyan has kept watch at the gates of Tevildo's fortress since the early days. None may pass without his leave, and his keen eyes miss nothing. Many a prisoner has been dragged past him into the dark halls within, never to emerge again. He delights in the slow torment of those who think themselves clever enough to slip by.
Murrik, the Doorkeeper has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

The Iron Crown of Morgoth Bauglir, wrought in Angband to hold the stolen light of the world. One socket gapes empty and dark, but in the other two burn still two Silmarils—jewels of Fëanor, containing the imperishable light of the Two Trees. They are the greatest treasures remaining in Middle-earth, and war and ruin have followed in their wake.
The regent's crown assembly is a brutal housing for the stolen dawnseeds. Its fastenings keep the power cells close to their captor while the tide cities wait for a working weather cycle.

Brother to Gilim, Nan is the giant of summer and the southern lands. Where Gilim brings frost, Nan brings scorching heat and withering drought. He towers like a great tree, and in his right hand he bears the longest blade you have ever seen. Both brothers swore allegiance to Melkor when the world was young, and both have served him ever since.
Borrath, the Giant has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

The Dragon-helm of Dor-lomin, forged by Telchar of Nogrod for Azaghal and given to Maedhros, who bestowed it upon Fingon. It passed to the House of Hador, and Túrin wore it when he was called the Dragon-helm. The servants of Morgoth fled before its terrible visage, for they deemed the spirit of the great worm Glaurung looked out from its eyes.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Cairn Banks'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift.

You stand now amid the ruined stones of a hidden city—Gondolin. Memory rushes fully clear: you fell here, defeating a Balrog, your life sacrificed to protect your people. Three powerful voices—Varda, Manwë, and Mandos—call to you clearly: "Rise again, Glorfindel, hero reborn. Morgoth's shadow stirs once more—your light must stand against it."

At last you recognize Aster Quay. You are Eralen, the flood marshal who stayed behind to open its jammed relief gates. Your body was lost; the engine kept a damaged memoryprint. The Nine Custodians have recalled you because Varkesh has seized the dawnseeds that could restart the weather system.

The great axe of Tuor, son of Huor, wrought for him by the smiths of Gondolin. Its name is 'Thudder-sharp' for it strikes with the force of a club but cuts like a sword. Tuor wielded it in the Fall of Gondolin, where he slew Maeglin and cast him from the walls, and clove through countless orcs and trolls defending Idril and his son Eärendil.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Bulkhead'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. Its edge is especially dangerous to orcs. Its edge is especially dangerous to trolls. It is a bane to cinder fiends.

The great bow of Beleg Cuthalion, mightiest archer among all the Children of Ilúvatar. Made of black yew and strung with Beleg's own hair, which shimmers a pale gold. With this bow he guarded the marches of Doriath, until treachery and darkness brought his doom at his friend's own hand. When paired with Dailir, the bow's power awakens fully.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Reedbow'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council.

A glaive of mithril upon a shaft of dark Nan Elmoth wood, forged by the Noldor in their early years in Beleriand. 'Silver-cleaver' it is named in Sindarin, for its edge parts armour as easily as cloth. The blade feels alive and eager, granting unnatural speed and precision, but the fey spirit bound within it feeds on the wielder's strength.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Lumenhook'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. It helps the bearer resist being held. It is worked from lumesilver.

It appears as nothing more than a deepening of the darkness, a patch of shadow that moves against the feeble light. Yet something watches from within it, something that was perhaps once a living spirit before the dark craft of Morgoth's servants stripped it of all but malice and hunger. Its touch brings a darkness that no flame can dispel.

This shadow has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It is difficult to see with ordinary sight.

The fell hide of Draugluin, sire and lord of all the werewolves of Morgoth, slain by Huan the Hound of Valinor at Tol-in-Gaurhoth. He was the mightiest wolf that ever walked, yet even he fell before Huan and crept dying to his master's feet. Beren wore this hide to pass the gates of Angband, and its dread shape may still deceive the Enemy.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Grozhak'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. It aids quiet movement.

Son of Ulfang the Black, Uldor led the Easterling treachery in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad. At the height of battle, when victory seemed within reach, his host turned upon the sons of Fëanor. His betrayal doomed the Union of Maedhros and earned him eternal infamy. He was slain by Maglor, yet the curse upon his name endures: Uldor the Accursed.
Varrek, the Accursed has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

Thuringwethil, Woman of Secret Shadow, serves as messenger between Sauron on Tol-in-Gaurhoth and Morgoth in Angband. She is the mightiest of vampires, cloaked in an iron-barbed bat-fell that grants her the power of flight. Her beauty is a mask for terrible hunger, and her claws have torn the throats of many who trusted her charming guise.
Nerezza carries orders through ducts too narrow for ordinary couriers. The iron edges of her folded wings scrape the stone as she watches for an unguarded throat.

Leather armour fashioned from the hide of some great hunting cat of the wild, perhaps one of the fell beasts that served Tevildo, Prince of Cats, in the days before Huan humbled him. Its proportions seem strange, yet it fits perfectly when donned. The wearer moves with feline grace and feels a predator's desire to hunt awakening within.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Prowlerhide'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise.

Orcobal has risen through the ranks of Morgoth's orc-hosts by strength of arm and ruthless cunning. He bears scars from a hundred battles against the Eldar and commands the respect even of those captains who loathe him. His name is cursed in the songs of the Noldor, for he has slain many of their kin beneath the shadows of Thangorodrim.
Karzhek, Champion of the Orcs has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

From Eruman, the dark and frozen lands south of Valinor, came Gilim in the days when Melkor first raised his banner. He is a giant of winter, and frost follows in his wake. His breath freezes the air, and his footfalls shake the stone. Long has he served the Dark Lord, and long shall his name be cursed by those who dwell in the North.
Orrusk, the Giant of the Dry Crown has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

A young cold-drake, long and sinuous, coiling upon the stone floor. Scatha is cunning beyond his years, and has already begun to amass a hoard through theft and murder. His kind lack the fire of the Uruloki, but his claws are keen and his gaze holds a terrible power. One day he may crawl forth from Angband to trouble the world above.

Scatha the Worm has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety. Its breath carries freezing vapor. It can pin a victim in place. Its influence can cloud thought. Its presence can break courage.

Named for the great River Sirion that flowed through the heart of Beleriand, this glaive moves like its waters—ever restless, seeking every gap and opening. The Sirion was the mightiest river of those lands, and many realms rose and fell along its banks. In battle, this blade flows around defences and strikes where foes least expect.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the the Long Channel'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

The poisoned javelin of Eol the Dark Elf, forged in the shadows of Nan Elmoth. When Eol pursued Aredhel and Maeglin to Gondolin and Turgon denied him freedom, he hurled this spear at his son. Aredhel stepped before the blow, and none knew the point was poisoned until she died that night. For this murder Eol was cast from Caragdur.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Copper Thicket'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. It gathers darkness around its bearer. Its attacks carry venom.

The black sword Anglachel, forged by Eol of Nan Elmoth from star-iron. It was brought to Thingol in Doriath, and later borne by Beleg Cuthalion. Its edge is dreadful keen, and a cold will seems to wake when it is drawn. Many have found that mischance follows where this blade passes—as though it remembers every death it has dealt.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Nullblade'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It attracts danger. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons.

Ulfang the Black, chieftain of the Easterlings, swore false oaths of allegiance to the sons of Fëanor while secretly in the pay of Morgoth. His treachery in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad shattered the Union of Maedhros and condemned countless Eldar and Edain to death or slavery. He is cunning and ruthless, and strikes at every opening.
Zarvok the Black has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

A fire-drake of surpassing greed even among his avaricious kind, Smaug already hoards treasures stolen from Morgoth's own vaults. Young and ambitious, his golden scales gleam in the darkness as he surveys all he considers rightfully his. In ages to come he may grow into something truly terrible, but even now he is a deadly foe.
Ravaz has made a bed among sealed pressure vessels. Their polished brass pleases it almost as much as the prospect of roasting the next trespasser.

The Iron Crown of Morgoth Bauglir, forged in Angband to bear the three Silmarils, the stolen light of the Two Trees. Now all three jewels are gone, and the crown sits cold and empty—three dark sockets where stars once blazed, a monument to a glory stolen and a glory lost. Much of the Dark Lord's will was poured into its making.
The regent's crown assembly is a brutal housing for the stolen dawnseeds. Its fastenings keep the power cells close to their captor while the tide cities wait for a working weather cycle.

Last and mightiest child of Ungoliant the Gloomweaver, Shelob has inherited her mother's insatiable hunger for light. The darkness deepens wherever she dwells, for she drinks in all radiance to spin her webs of shadow. She has grown vast and terrible in the deep places of Angband, and all lesser spiders pay her fearful homage.
Trevethor, Spider of Darkness has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

The gleaming spear of Ingwe, High King of the Vanyar. Forged of mithril in Valinor, it is light as a feather yet stronger than steel. Though Ingwe sits forever at the feet of Manwë, this spear was borne by his son Ingwion in the War of Wrath, where it pierced the hearts of balrogs and cast down the dark towers of Thangorodrim.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Asten'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It carries a steady light. It is worked from lumesilver.

Gothmog, Lord of Balrogs, is the high-captain of Angband and marshal of the hosts of Morgoth. By his hand fell Fëanor and Fingon, High Kings of the Noldor, and never yet has he been mastered in battle. With whips of flame he and his demons drove Ungoliant from their master, when Morgoth's cry rang through the trembling North.
Korrav commands the cinder companies. Heat bleeds from his armor, and his whip has left permanent channels in the floor.

The crown of Maedhros, High King of the Noldor, who was captured by Morgoth and hung by his right hand from Thangorodrim. The weight of the Oath of Fëanor rests heavily upon it, a curse that drives its wearer to doom even as it grants them kingly will. When worn with his hauberk, one feels the full measure of his endurance.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Rethan'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It attracts danger.

A mithril helm rising to a tall spike, worn by Ecthelion, Lord of the Fountains of Gondolin. When the city fell, he faced Gothmog, Lord of Balrogs, and drove the spike into the demon's breast as they plunged together into the Fountain of the King. Both perished, but the helm still echoes with the music of falling water.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Cevran'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial.

The crown of Daeron the Minstrel, loremaster of Doriath and inventor of the Cirth, the runes of Middle-earth. His songs were reckoned second only to those of the Ainur, though his love for Lúthien was unrequited. '...Daeron the Dark with ferny crown played with bewildering wizard's art music for breaking of the heart.'

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Lysven'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing.

The sable sword reforged from Anglachel, wielded by Túrin. Its blade can slice iron like parchment, and it drinks deeply of blood. A fell curse  lies upon it: once unsheathed, it must taste blood. The sword's grim will  fills its master with fearless despair, drawing mighty foes nigh—and  giving strength to slay them.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Debtkeeper'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. Its hungry work draws vitality from wounds. It attracts danger. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons.

A suit of mail once worn by Maedhros, eldest son of Fëanor. Stripped from him when he was hung from Thangorodrim, it was stored in Morgoth's iron vaults. It is stained with the memory of torment and the unbreakable Oath that drives Fëanor's kin. When worn with his crown, one feels the full measure of his endurance.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Rethan'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. It guards against fire. It helps resist venom.

Belegwath is wreathed in darkness deeper than the pits of Angband, yet within that shadow burns a terrible flame. His great wings of night unfold to blot out all light, and he moves through the halls like doom itself. For many of the Children of Ilúvatar, this Mighty Shadow has been the last thing they ever beheld.
Vozhrek, cinder fiend of Shadow has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

Tevildo is a mighty fay in the service of Melko, lord and master of all the cats. In his fortress he keeps many thralls in torment, and his hatred of the Hound of Valinor is legendary. His strength lies partly in a golden collar about his neck wherein a spell is locked, and while he wears it, none may defeat him.
Razzek rules the furnace cats from a nest of stolen cushions and crew uniforms. The title is his own invention; the claws are real enough.

A hammer wrought by Aulë himself in the days following the destruction of the Two Trees, and carried from Valinor by mighty Rog, Lord of the House of the Hammer of Wrath. It has a haft and head of black iron banded about with red gold and strikes with earth-shattering force, sundering armour and bone alike.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Korren's Wrath'. Its maker marked the underside with a tide gauge rather than a signature. It passed through the evacuation stores and was recovered from a sealed cargo lift. Its presence draws hostile attention. It attracts danger. It is a bane to cinder fiends.

Among the cold-drakes of the North, Gostir is most feared for his terrible gaze. Those who meet his eyes are held fast as though bound by invisible chains, unable to flee as doom approaches. Though he lacks the fire of his kin, his hypnotic stare has claimed more victims than many a flame-breathing wyrm.

Ozhar, the Dread Glance has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety. It can pin a victim in place. Its influence can cloud thought. Its presence can break courage.

The 'Foe-hammer', forged by Enerdhil of Gondolin and borne by Turgon, King of the Hidden City. Its edge is the bane of orcs, trolls, dragons, and Balrogs alike. It is the mate to Orcrist, the Goblin-cleaver, and when both blades are wielded together, they sing in harmony as they did in the Elder Days.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Gateknell'. A route code is scratched where only its bearer would see it. The code leads to a maintenance station missing from current maps. Its edge is especially dangerous to orcs. Its edge is especially dangerous to trolls. Its edge is especially dangerous to dragons. It is a bane to cinder fiends.

An orc-lord of great cunning, who has served Morgoth long enough to have earned his master's favour. His massive frame is clad in heavy armour, and he wields both sword and whip with equal skill. His cruelty to subordinates and prisoners alike has earned him a feared name among the hosts of Angband.
Othrod, the Orc Lord has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

A huge champion of the orcs, clad in thick black armour and bearing a shield and much-notched axe. Scarred and baleful, Balcmeg earned his name for the way he pursues his prey -- he never stops, never rests, and none who flee from him have ever reached safety. His warband follows him out of dread.
Drezhak, the Relentless has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

A small and exceptionally ugly orc, the most twisted of Morgoth's mockeries. Despite his wretched appearance, Lug moves with a dexterity that belies his form, tossing his short broad blade from hand to hand. His strikes land in places that wound most deeply, and few survive his attentions long.
Ozzek, the Grotesque has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

By silver waters Elves first woke
beneath the stars ere morning broke.
No sun had risen, no moon shone —
just heaven's light on lake and stone.

Then Morgoth's shadow veiled the land
and stole the Light with iron hand.
Yet still a whisper stirs the deep:
what darkness took, the bold may reap.

The cities were built around tide gauges,
with gardens above their cisterns.
The engine measured every storm
and told the ferries when to leave.

Then the command lines were seized.
The forecasts stopped, the gates stayed shut.
Somewhere beneath the shattered quays
the old equipment still runs.

The winged cloak of Thuringwethil, the vampire-messenger of Sauron who flew between Angband and Tol-in-Gaurhoth. Lúthien wore this fell garment to enter the throne room of Morgoth himself. Its great black wings still hold dark power, and servants of the Enemy may mistake its wearer for kin.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Nerezza'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. It aids quiet movement.

A Balrog who has earned his rank not by terror alone, but by the winning of battles. Turkano commands a host of lesser Raukar with cold authority, and under his leadership they have broken armies of the Eldar upon the slopes of Thangorodrim. His sword burns with a flame older than the Sun.
Zhavrek, cinder fiend of the Hosts has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

The Nauglamir; a carcanet of gold set with a multitude of shining gems of Valinor, made by the Dwarves of Ered Luin for Finrod Felagund. It is the most renowned work of their craft in the Elder Days, and despite its weight of gold and jewels it lies upon the neck light as a strand of flax.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Stormchain'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact. It helps the bearer resist being held.

Out of the pits of Angband there issued the winged dragons, that had not before been seen; and so sudden and ruinous was the onset of that dreadful fleet that the host of the Valar was driven back, for the coming of the dragons was with great thunder, and lightning, and a tempest of fire.
Vorrakash fills the overhead service void. Its furnace breath could turn the suspended walkways into falling streams of metal.

Leather armour worn by Haldad, chieftain of the Haladin and father of Haleth the Hunter. He fell defending his people when orcs besieged them in the stockade at the confluence of the Ascar and Gelion. Hardened by that desperate stand, it lends courage to those who must hold the line.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Jorven'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It helps the bearer resist being held.

The unerring arrow of Beleg Cuthalion, greatest archer of the Sindar. 'Dailir' means 'the Returner', for this arrow would always be found again after it was shot, no matter how far it flew. Beleg treasured it above all his arrows. When loosed from Belthronding, its power is greatest.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Trueflight'. This was carried out of the breach inside an ordinary tool crate. Generations of careful repair have kept the original work intact.

A deep green robe patterned with gold, once worn by Andreth the Wise, a mortal woman of Beor's House who debated with Finrod Felagund on the fate of Men and Elves. Though she loved Aegnor and was loved in return, they were sundered by the doom of their kinds. It sharpens the senses.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Sevra'. It bears the inventory mark of a relief ferry that never reached the outer banks. Someone brought it back, but left no account of the crossing.

In Valinor the Two Trees shone
with gold and silver, leaf and bough.
Their mingled light is dead and gone —
the world lies under shadow now.

Across the ice the exiles came,
the Noldor burning with their oath.
They traded bliss for grief and flame
and lost the blessing of them both.

The upper reservoirs once shared
the work of feeding cloud and rain.
Their pipelines crossed a hundred miles
of marsh, bridge, garden, and quay.

Now the pumps answer to one crown.
The crews are scattered, the charts incomplete.
You return with tools and broken memories
to restore what can still be used.

The immense, blackened steel axe of Gothmog, Lord of Balrogs and High Captain of Angband. Flames crawl along its edge, and it strikes with such force that it can hew down many foes in a single sweep. The weapon burns with an evil will, rousing wrath and noise, loath to be put aside.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Korrav'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. Its presence draws hostile attention. Its attacks carry flame.

The mail of Gundor, eldest son of Hador Goldenhead, who fell alongside his father at Eithel Sirion defending the rearguard of Fingolfin in the Dagor Bragollach. Though young, he slew many before he was overcome. This corslet grants strength to those who must stand against many foes.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Garrek'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial.

This shield bears the device of the Blessed Realm, wrought in the light of the Two Trees before the Darkening. It shines like the full moon upon the sea, a memory of Valinor when all was unmarred. Those who bear it feel the peace of the Undying Lands, and their hearts are gladdened.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the High Reservoir'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It carries a steady light.

Before the Sun and Moon were wrought
the Eldar walked by starlight alone.
Now shadow stirs beneath the earth
where Morgoth sits upon his throne.

Three jewels blaze upon his crown —
stolen fire none may reclaim...
unless one dares the iron dark
and walks through everlasting flame.

The tide clocks have stopped.
No forecast reaches the empty docks.
Below them a stolen engine
still serves a single ruler.

Three dawnseeds can restore it.
They are small enough to carry,
if you can reach the crown assembly
and find your way back out.

A shining blue shield set with crystals, borne by Fingolfin, High King of the Noldor, when he rode alone to challenge Morgoth before the gates of Angband. Seven times he wounded the Dark Lord with Ringil ere he fell, and Morgoth went ever after halt of one foot from those wounds.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Brennek'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It carries a steady light.

A slender, gilded sword once wielded by Idril Celebrindal, Princess of Gondolin. She alone foresaw the city's doom and prepared the secret way of escape. The blade gleams with golden light, lending courage and grace to its bearer, and no snare or enchantment can easily hold them.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Sereth'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It helps the bearer resist being held.

The 'dark-slayer'; a blade borne by Beren son of Barahir through the perils of Nan Dungortheb and into the pits of Angband itself. With this sword he fought beside the Hound of Valinor against the servants of Morgoth. It sheds a pale light that heartens the bearer in dark places.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'Gloamcleft'. The pattern was approved for a rescue unit, then copied without permission by a private armory. This example retains the older workshop seal. It carries a steady light.

A shadowy cloak woven by Lúthien Tinúviel from her own dark hair, which grew past her heels. With this garment and her enchanting song she cast Morgoth himself into slumber in the depths of Angband. Its folds deepen the shadows around the wearer and lull the watchful into sleep.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Nysara'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise. It aids quiet movement.

A helm worn by Curufin, fifth son of Fëanor and most like his father in skill of hand and cunning of mind. He was a master smith, yet his scheming brought ruin to Finrod's realm. The helm sharpens the wearer's craft and guile, but its treacherous whispers can never be silenced.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Veskir'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening. It attracts danger. It aids quiet movement.

An ancient cold-drake of immense size, lacking the fire of the Uruloki but no less deadly for it. Its hypnotic gaze can freeze prey in place, and its claws and fangs have slain countless warriors. It has grown cunning beyond mortal understanding over long centuries of darkness.

This great cold-drake has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It can pin a victim in place. Its influence can cloud thought. Its presence can break courage.

Barely hatched from the fire-pits where Morgoth breeds his wyrms, this young drake is already as large as a man. Thin wisps of smoke curl from its nostrils, and its scales still have the soft gleam of youth. Yet even now its breath carries flame enough to sear flesh from bone.

This fire-drake hatchling has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat.

A delicate necklace traced with intricate designs, once worn by Tinfang Gelion, the Piper, a mysterious spirit of the twilight woods. His flute-playing could bind even the nightingales to silence. To wear this amulet is to hear the echo of Elvish music and long for starlight.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Chimekeeper Vell'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial.

A great Uruloki, fire-drake of Angband, grown vast and terrible over centuries of slaughter. Its breath is a torrent of flame that can melt stone, and its scales gleam like hot coals. It has amassed a hoard worthy of its terrible power, for who could ever challenge a Dragon?

This great fire-drake has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat. It can pin a victim in place. Its presence can break courage.

The very largest and toughest of the trolls are chosen for the personal guard of Gothmog, High Captain of Angband. Drilled relentlessly for war, they wear armour wrought in the forges below and bear weapons that can shatter stone. Nothing short of death itself can stop them.
This troll guard has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

Before you stands Nienna, the Lady of Pity, she who mourns for every hurt that Arda has suffered. Her tears watered the dying Trees, and those who hearken to her learn pity, and endurance in hope. Her gaze rests upon you, grave and gentle, full of grief that is not despair.
Ilyra waits by a sheltered return line. Her equipment is worn from repairing damage the other custodians cannot bear to examine.

Oromë the Great stands before you, Lord of Forests, the Huntsman of the Valar, who in the youth of the world hunted the monsters of Morgoth by starlight. The dread of him lies upon all cruel things, and the echo of his horn Valaróma is a terror to every servant of the dark.
Veylan listens through a bundle of hunting wires. The movements of creatures in distant passages reach his instruments as faint, distinct clicks.

A heavy coat of mail from the hill of Amon Rudh, where the Petty-dwarves once dwelt in their hidden halls. Túrin Turambar sheltered there with his outlaws, until treachery brought ruin. The armour carries the stubbornness of that doomed hill, where defiance outlasted hope.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Red Pump'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council.

The hunting knife of Mablung of Doriath, captain of Thingol's guard. After Carcharoth was slain in the Hunting of the Wolf, Mablung cut the Silmaril from the beast's belly with this blade. Its edge is pitiless against wolves, and it lends the keen-eyed focus of its master.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Torren'. A repair ticket is still caught beneath one fitting. Whoever finished the work returned it to service instead of waiting for the inspection council. It is a bane to wolves.

Fragments of golden radiance flash clearly in your memory—hair like sunlit gold, a fall amidst flames, cheers of saved souls. Your identity nearly emerges, bright yet elusive. Calmness washes over you like deep sleep, the healing dreams of Irmo gently restoring your mind.
Sleep brings the smell of rain on hot masonry. You see your old marshal coat hanging beside a tide chart, but wake before you can read the marked date.

A champion risen from the brutal fighting-pits of Angband, where orcs prove themselves before Morgoth's captains. He bears scars from countless bouts and wears well-crafted armour, his battle axe notched and stained dark with the blood of his own kind as much as any foe.
This orc champion has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

A red-winged drake descended from Ancalagon's first storm out of Angband, greater and swifter than the crawling Uruloki below. Heat ripples from its ember-bright scales, and its breath breaks forth as a pure torrent of furnace flame when it plunges from the vaults above.

This flying fire-drake has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat.

An Orc captain hardened by years of raids against the Eldar, Baugon rules his warband through fear. He takes pride in prisoners brought alive to Angband, and his followers know what awaits those who fail him. His cruel strength is an Orc's own, with no spirit behind it.
Krask, the Merciless has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

Before you stands Mandos, the Doomsman of the Valar, keeper of the Houses of the Dead, who forgets nothing that has been and speaks only the counsels of Ilúvatar. His presence is solemn beyond all speech, and in his eyes is the memory of every doom that has been spoken.
Nareth carries the recall ledger. Each entry records a life the engine tried to bring back, the power it spent, and what could not be recovered.

One of the eldest surviving spawn of Ungoliant the Gloomweaver, this ancient spider has grown vast and cunning over countless years. Its bloated body drips with venom so potent that even dragons fear its bite. It has lurked in darkness since before the Sun first rose.
This ancient spider has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

The mightiest of the great serpents, armoured in scales of adamant that no blade forged by mortal hands may cut. Prismatic colours gleam and shift across its flanks as it breathes forth fire, cold, poison, and shadow in turn. It is said to be as old as Angband itself.

This ancient adamant serpent has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat. Its breath carries freezing vapor. Its breath extinguishes light.

A twisted growth born of Morgoth's malice, this thorn-plant draws the very light from the air around it, leaving only cold darkness in its wake. It was first found creeping through the lightless halls of Angband, and has since spread its roots through many a cavern.
This nightthorn has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

The White Lady of the Noldor once wore this robe, cut of the finest white cloth and hemmed with silver thread. Aredhel loved to ride and hunt in the wild lands, and though Eol ensnared her in Nan Elmoth, the robe remembers her freedom and quickens the wearer's step.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Perya'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It helps the bearer resist being held. It attracts danger.

The famed shield of Hador Goldenhead, Lord of Dor-lomin and greatest chieftain of the Edain. His house was blessed by the Eldar, and the golden light of his hair passed to his descendants. This shield withstood the fires of Angband and the bitter cold of the North.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Garven'. Its fittings were made to be serviced with common workshop tools. Behind that modest design lies a standard the later foundries rarely matched. It guards against fire. It guards against cold.

Chief among the thanes of Tevildo, Oikeroi is sworn to guard his master with fang and claw. He is cunning in the ways of ambush and has slain many who sought to challenge the Prince of Cats. His loyalty to Tevildo is absolute, born of both fear and dark devotion.
Keshak, Guard of Razzek has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

An archer of the Easterling host, sworn to Morgoth's service. His people came to Beleriand under fair words, but their allegiance was bought with dark promises. He draws his bow with practiced ease, and his arrows have felled many an Elven lord from the shadows.
This banklander archer has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

Gorgol earned his title through the butchery of captives, a spectacle he uses to keep his warband in terror of his wrath. He is large for an orc-captain and wields a heavy cleaver stained dark with old blood. His pack follows him out of fear rather than loyalty.
Urzhek, the Butcher has claimed a station in the broken weather works. The marks of earlier intruders remain nearby, a practical warning against mistaking silence for safety.

This great wyrm has coiled in the frozen depths of Angband since before the rising of the Sun. Its sapphire scales gleam with an inner frost, and the air crystallises around it in glittering motes. Its breath can freeze a warrior where he stands, armour and all.

This ancient sapphire serpent has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath carries freezing vapor.

A ring that once graced the hand of Melian, a Maia who dwelt in the gardens of Lórien before she came to Middle-earth and wedded Thingol in Doriath. Her power wove the Girdle that kept the realm hidden from all evil, and the ring holds an echo of her foresight.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Meyra'. This belonged to a crew assigned to the deepest pressure locks. Its surface is worn by practical use, while the concealed workmanship remains precise.

The bow of Celegorm the Fair, third son of Fëanor, who in the days of Valinor hunted with Oromë the Great. The Vala gifted him Huan, the Hound of Valinor. But the Oath drove Celegorm to terrible deeds, and the bow clings to its bearer as the curse clung to him.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Casken'. A small hollow once held a written order. The paper is gone, but its edges left a pale rectangle beneath the fastening.

A warrior of the Easterlings, one of those peoples who crossed into Beleriand and swore oaths to the lords of the Eldar -- only to break them when Morgoth's promises proved sweeter. He fights with a crude blade and a shield, loyal now only to the Dark Lord.
This banklander warrior has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

Grown vast in the furnaces of Angband where it has basked since the world was young, this serpent's ruby scales glow as though lit from within. Wisps of smoke curl from its nostrils and the extreme heat it radiates makes the very air painful to breathe.

This ancient ruby serpent has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. Its breath is a rush of furnace heat.

A spirit of fire given terrible form, blazing so fiercely that its shape is hard to discern. Like Arien who guides the Sun, it was once a spirit of flame, but it chose to follow Melkor when the World was young, and now its fire serves only to destroy.
This ember revenant has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

A troll bred in the deepest pits of Angband, where no light has ever reached. Its hide is grey as wet stone and its limbs are thick and powerful, shaped by ages in the crushing dark. It fears the light, and fights all the more savagely for that fear.
This cave troll has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

One of the warriors of Tevildo's court, this great cat walks upright like a man, though no man could match its speed. Its long scything claws are weapons of terrible precision, and it moves with a fluid grace that makes it nearly impossible to track.
This cat warrior has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

When Turgon departed Vinyamar in Nevrast, he left this armour, and strange destiny has led it far from those halls. It is crafted with a double layer of mail, which makes it too heavy for many, but turns blows that might cleave through a lesser suit.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of the Western Catchment'. Its pattern was developed in a workshop above a hot return pipe. The uneven finishing records many interrupted nights of work.

A faded presence that perhaps once was man or elf, now bound to the world of shadow by dark arts wrought in Morgoth's service. It moves unseen through the halls, and those who feel its touch are seized by a terror from which reason cannot free them.

This phantom has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It is difficult to see with ordinary sight.

A Rauko of shadow and darkness, among the first spirits to fall when Melkor raised his banner in defiance of Ilúvatar. It moves through the halls like a creeping void, and its touch brings a darkness so deep that even torches cannot burn within it.
This shade revenant has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

You glimpse yourself wielding a sword with graceful mastery—swift, precise, radiant. Your spirit swells with pride and confidence, yet the moment is fleeting. Petals dance unseen around you, a subtle touch from ever-young Vana, honoring your grace.
Green light spills from a cracked culture tank. Its stored warmth reaches you, and a memory returns of the gardens built above the old seawall.

Your spirit recalls death, sacrifice—but also purpose beyond defeat. Gentle yet majestic voices whisper in harmony: "Even death cannot silence your courage. Rise once more." Radiance pierces darkness—starlight and sky, blessings of Varda and Manwë.
The custodians restore a shared power bus. Your scattered memories briefly meet: rescue, duty, a flood rising too quickly. They ask you to continue.

A sudden pulse of self-sacrifice fills your heart—a moment when you willingly traded your life for others. Your spirit trembles at the strength of that choice. Quick, joyful steps echo beside you, invisible yet clear—Nessa's fleet encouragement.
Your feet find balance on a narrow maintenance rail. You remember carrying a child across such a gap, with a rope tied around both your waists.

Vague shapes of companions appear briefly, allies of various races—faces blurred, names lost. Yet loyalty and friendship resonate deep within. The gentle scent of new leaves fills your senses, a subtle gift from Yavanna, encouraging remembrance.
A shoot grows through a corroded joint. Thessa has kept one nursery alive. You remember people passing seed trays hand to hand as the tide rose.

One of the silent hunters of Tevildo's court, this jet-black cat moves through shadow as though born of it. Unseen and patient, it looses its cruel arrows from the dark with the calm precision of one who has stalked and slain many times before.
