This cat assassin has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It is difficult to see with ordinary sight.

Your fingers trace flowing runes carved gently into stone walls. The symbols resonate with warmth, though you cannot yet read them clearly. Delicate threads of silver glimmer faintly—Vairë, the Weaver, slowly restoring your fractured memories.
Ilyra threads a new connection through the recall loom. A face nearly forms in the static: someone who trusted you with the evacuation keys.

A Rauko of mist and poisoned air, one of the subtler servants of Morgoth. It drifts unseen through the halls of Angband, a creeping miasma of malice. Those it engulfs are filled with visions of such horror that their minds shatter like glass.

This mist revenant has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter. It is difficult to see with ordinary sight.

A giant of Morgoth's hosts, as tall as three men and armed with a massive club. These brutes served the Dark Lord since before the rising of the Sun, and their strength is terrible to behold. They hurl great boulders at their foes from afar.
This giant has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

Here stands Tulkas the Strong, last of the Powers to come down into Arda and mightiest in deeds of strength. He bears no weapon, for his hands are weapon enough, and his laughter rings against the stone until dust falls from the unseen roof.
Drevan has disconnected his outer armor to work in the narrow service shaft. The machinery he lifts each day weighs more than any weapon.

A cruel Easterling who ruled Dor-lomin with an iron fist after the Nirnaeth Arnoediad. He oppressed the people of Húrin's house and was foretold to die by Túrin's blade, but fate has been altered. The dark power binds his spirit here still.
Borruk rules the captive labor crews. This false body has been rebuilt around a stolen memoryprint; destroying it may free what remains of the person inside.

Beyond the Walls of the World lies the Void, the Outer Dark into which Morgoth shall at the last be thrust through the Door of Night. For one breath you stand upon its threshold, where there is no star, no song, no name, and no returning.
Beyond the last service hatch is a silent chamber with no return cable. You stand at its threshold and feel the engine lose your position.

You feel again the iron of Angband—the weight that bowed even Húrin, chained upon the heights to watch his kin destroyed. No fetter binds your limbs, yet something heavier settles on the will, and each rising costs you more than the last.
You remember holding the tide doors against their own weight. Each return now asks the same effort of your mind.

A spirit bound still to the earth by necromancy wrought in Morgoth's service, wrapped in a rotting shroud. It guards the treasures that were laid with it in the grave, and the touch of its withered hand saps the strength from living flesh.
This grave wight has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

The largest of the venomous serpents bred in Angband's deepest pits, its emerald scales shimmer sickly in the gloom. It moves within a billowing cloud of poisonous vapour so thick that merely breathing near it can bring sickness and death.
This ancient emerald serpent has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

An orc trained in the use of the short bow, a weapon copied crudely from the Eldar. He looses his arrows from the safety of darkness, and though his aim lacks the grace of the firstborn, numbers and malice make up for what skill does not.
This orc archer has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

One of the lesser spirits that fell with Morgoth, this Rauko has chosen the cold rather than the flame as its domain. A chill hangs heavy in the air around it, and the pale gleaming blade in its hand drinks the warmth from all it touches.
This rime revenant has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

Far below, a vast laughter rises—slow, and cold, and certain—the mirth of the Dark Lord who deems the last light quenched at last. The Silmarils burn unseen in his iron crown; and for this hour, in this place, the world is wholly his.
Varkesh shuts down the final relief channel. The dawnseeds remain locked in his crown assembly, while the cities above wait for a weather cycle that does not begin.

Thread by thread you feel yourself drawn out of the Music, the great Song in which all things were sung into being. What Ilúvatar wove, the Enemy would unweave; and for a moment you cannot recall the shape that you were meant to hold.
The recall loom begins discarding damaged connections. A lifetime becomes a set of useful movements, then fewer movements still.

Dim images drift through your mind: stone halls, green forests, lands bathed in starlight. You feel deeply drawn to them, yet cannot grasp why. Above, the brief glimmer of distant stars—Varda's silent eyes—remind you of forgotten hope.
An amber indicator flashes behind the stone. Solen, keeper of the failing lamps, has found your return signal. For a moment you remember a city reflected in floodwater.

Your last cry goes out into the stone and returns to you smaller, and smaller still, until the dark has swallowed even the memory of it. No song will carry this ending westward. It is simply unmade, as though it had never been begun.
Your call reaches the end of a conduit and returns as a dull click. No recording survives long enough to identify the speaker.

A spirit chained to the earth by dark enchantment, unable to pass into the halls of Mandos. It haunts its burial chamber wrapped in tattered grave-cloths, and the cold that seeps from it is a cold of the soul, not merely of the flesh.
This barrow wight has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

The fire the Powers kindled in your spirit burns low now, like a forge left untended through a long and starless night. Each fall has cost you a little of its warmth, and the cold of Angband leans close to drink what little remains.
The return chamber warms slowly. Its reserve has fallen low enough that even the warning chime sounds tired.

You feel weight upon your shoulders, like armor worn proudly. A fragment of bravery stirs within you, an echo of battles faced with courage. A joyful strength fills your limbs—the unseen presence of laughing Tulkas urging you onward.
Pressure builds beneath your feet. Drevan steadies the return platform, and you remember standing your ground while others crossed a shaking bridge.

The shadow that lies upon all the North no longer waits without; it has found the way within, and coils about your heart like cold smoke. It gives no command. It only suggests, almost gently, that surrender would be a kind of rest.
A faulty contact feeds the return loop back into itself. You hear your own doubts repeated until they sound like instructions.

An Elf-wrought knife, finely balanced and keen. It was a birthday-gift that Húrin Thalion gave to his son Túrin, and Túrin bore it through many hard years. It lends steadiness of heart and a stubborn refusal to be ensnared or held.

This surviving work of the reservoir workshops bears the inscription 'of Drennar'. It was commissioned with the last payment from a drowned district. The maker refused to turn a difficult promise into a cheap memorial. It helps the bearer resist being held.

You stand upon grey ash where green things should grow, as upon Anfauglith, the choking dust that was a fair and grassy plain before the fires came. Nothing you set here will take root. The very earth has forgotten how to answer.
Salt covers the abandoned nursery beds. Thessa can preserve seed, but nothing will grow until fresh water returns.

A bat twisted by Morgoth's power into something feral and unnatural. Its wings are black as the void, and it hunts in the lightless deeps with a shriek that chills the blood. Even in darkness, it finds its prey with uncanny ease.
This shadow bat has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

A bat warped beyond all natural shape by Morgoth's corruption. Its head is grotesquely misshapen, with long curving fangs that drain the very strength from the flesh they pierce. It moves with a speed that belies its broken form.
This twisted bat has adapted to the abandoned service passages. It watches the path between you and the nearest shelter, ready to turn a careless approach into a dangerous encounter.

An attercop -- poison-spider, as the folk call it -- as big as a hound, covered in thick dark bristles. It spins webs of deathly silk to entangle the unwary, and its pale bulbous eyes gleam with a hunger that is almost knowing.
